LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch, what to know and a prediction as Jacksonville heads to Baltimore to open Week 9 Imagn Images In the Week 9 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Baltimore Ravens play host to the Jacksonville Jaguars . Baltimore is coming off a devastating loss to the Buffalo Bills in which Lamar Jackson returned from his ankle injury and was promptly injured on his first play of the game. The Ravens also lost backup Tyler Huntley during the contest, and they are now decimated on offense as they head into Thursday night's game. Jacksonville came off its bye last week and laid the smack down on the division rival Indianapolis Colts , winning 42-7 to improve to 5-2 on the season and further solidify their hold on the AFC South. Trevor Lawrence and the offense are rolling, and the defense has been largely excellent so far this year. Will the Jaguars take care of business on the road, or will the Ravens pull off a shocking upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Ravens vs. Jaguars live Date: Thursday, Nov. 5 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: M&T Bank Stadium (Baltimore) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Jaguars -9.5, O/U 39.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Jaguars have the ball The Jags enter this game having destroyed the Colts last week behind a monster performance from their running game. Bhayshul Tuten ran 16 times for 104 yards and a touchdown, while Chris Rodriguez carried it six times for 41 yards and another score. Rodriguez was limited in practice this week with a hand injury but will play on Thursday night. Tuten's status is up in the air after he didn't practice all week due to an ankle injury sustained against Indianapolis. He played through that injury for the rest of the game, but Jacksonville might choose to rest him here. He's a game-time decision. The Ravens are allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season, with a mere 0.8 of those yards coming before contact, according to Tru Media. Jacksonville could have some issues running the ball, especially if Tuten is out, if the Baltimore front can hold up as it has for most of the season. The Ravens did get clocked for 146 yards on the ground this past week by the Bills, but James Cook averaged south of 4.0 yards per carry. A lot of the damage was done by Ray Davis late in the game with six carries for 30 yards. Josh Allen also chipped in 30 of his own. Trevor Lawrence obviously isn't as mobile or as involved in the run game as Allen, but he can move, and if the Ravens get out of their rushing lanes, he can make things happen as a scrambler. Lawrence has played extremely well so far this season, completing 65.7% of his passes at an average of 8.5 yards per attempt, with 17 touchdowns (and a league-high 8.6% touchdown rate) against just four interceptions. Lawrence's top target is clearly Parker Washington , who splits his time fairly evenly between lining up out wide and in the slot. The Ravens are 21st in net yards per attempt allowed this season, and their cornerbacks ( Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins ) largely haven't played up to expectations. Kyle Hamilton remains excellent against both the run and pass in the slot, so one could expect Washington's route split to lean more heavily toward the outside. Jacksonville may lean toward putting him where he can line up against Humphrey, whose struggles this season have been fairly well documented. Elsewhere on the perimeter, Jakobi Meyers and, to a lesser extent, Brian Thomas Jr . and Josh Cameron are involved. Meyers and Thomas have only combined for three more targets than Washington has, though, so they are more clearly ancillary pieces in the passing game. The box-score expectations for them should be somewhat muted, but they can pop up at any time for key plays. (Thomas did score last week in his return to the full-time WR3 role, for example.) The Ravens, meanwhile, have been relatively stingy against tight ends in the passing game, allowing only 35 receptions to players at the position, so it's probably not going to be the biggest night for Brenton Strange . Tight ends do have six touchdowns against the Ravens, though, so it might be worth it to at least watch out for Strange in the red zone. When the Ravens have the ball You can throw out all of the Ravens' offensive stats. Not only is Lamar Jackson out, but so is backup quarterback Tyler Huntley. Jacoby Brissett is reportedly on the way to help, but he won't be active on Thursday night. Emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano entered the game in relief of Jackson and Huntley last Sunday and will make the start on Thursday night. Fagnano, an undrafted free agent out of UConn, went 10-of-21 for 91 yards and an interception against the Bills. He threw most of his passes to the running backs and did not connect with Zay Flowers even once. Expect the Ravens to lean heavily on Derrick Henry and the run game, but do not expect them to find much success. Henry has been struggling of late to begin with (45 carries for 156 yards and a touchdown over the last three games combined), and the Jaguars have allowed 3.4 yards per carry this season — the single-best mark in all of football. Unless Fagnano and offensive coordinator Declan Doyle pull off some kind of magic act, the Ravens are likely not going to be able to move the ball much on Thursday night. The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Now Playing Share Share Video Does Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore have any chance in 'TNF' matchup? Joe Fagnano got the start because Lamar Jackson is on injured reserve with a right thumb problem, and the NFL says he'll miss at least four games. Baltimore now sits last in the AFC North. Robert Griffin III saw the game and posted a two-sentence take that Ravens fans can't stop arguing about. His timing, and his point, deserve a closer look. Joe Fagnano Had No Easy Way To Follow Lamar Jackson The division race isn't waiting around. The Pittsburgh Steelers are 6-2, the Cincinnati Bengals are 5-2, and the Ravens are two and a half games behind Pittsburgh. A month without Jackson could push them out of the picture entirely. The next game is against the Los Angeles Chargers on November 16. That's a chance to grab a win before the schedule toughens, but only if Fagnano protects the ball and the defense gets stops early. Baltimore needs a calm opening drive more than a spectacular one. Fans will be watching for signs that Thursday was a one-off. If the offense stalls again, the questions about this season will get louder fast, and the front office will hear them too. away.headline: Jaguars-Ravens Injury Report: Why Recent History Doesn't Bode Well for Bhayshul Tuten
away.blurb: The Jaguars released their final injury report for Thursday's Week 9 battle with the Baltimore Ravens, and it featured two big names as questionable: running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker. There is understandable concern for both, with Walker limited in practice on Tuesday and Wednesday after sustaining a rib injury in last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts. But recent history under this Jaguars regime suggests Walker has at least a chance to play. It does not say the same about Tuten. Simply put, the Jaguars will more than likely need Chris Rodriguez Jr. to step into a starting role on Thursday based on how they have handled past injury situations. Tuten did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday, despite Jaguars head coach Liam Coen indicating in his pre-practice press conference that Tuten would have some sort of practice activity. Instead, Tuten was a DNP for the second day in a row, which has resulted in a missed game each time during the Coen era. This is the 25th game where the Jaguars are led by Coen and his staff. In the previous 24 final injury reports, the Jaguars have had 27 instances where a player did not practice during the week. In all 27 of those instances, the player missed the game that week. The key difference here is that Tuten is at least listed as questionable. All 27 previous instances of players missing practice led to them being outright ruled out, which of course has not been the case with Tuten. Coen has already tabbed Tuten as a game-time decision, something he has done two other times this year: in Week 1 with Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen, who were each listed as questionable but played. The difference is that Van Lanen and Allen at least practiced that week. If this was a full week and not a Thursday Night Game, which the Jaguars have not played under Coen before, perhaps things would be different. But for now, most signs point toward Tuten not being available just simply based on the Jaguars' history under Coen. Perhaps one key that could answer the Tuten question is how Coen approached Van Lanen's status in Week 1. Van Lanen was coming off a serious knee injury that had kept him out of the entirety of training camp, though he returned in time to be limited in practice in Week 1. But a few weeks before then, here is what Coen had to say. home.headline: Desperate Baltimore Ravens seal huge NFL quarterback trade after Jackson and Huntley injuries
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens have found a fix to their quarterback injury woes by trading for Arizona Cardinals star Jacoby Brissett. The Ravens are down to third-choice undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano ahead of Thursday night's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars , leaving general manager Eric DaCosta desperately scrabbling around for a long-term solution. NFL insider Ian Rapoport was the first to report on Wednesday that the Ravens are now finalizing a trade for Brissett, with the deal set to be completed over the weekend. Fagnano will therefore be on the field for Baltimore on Thursday night, before Brissett takes the quarterback reins in Week 10 for the Monday Night Football showdown against the winless Los Angeles Chargers. Brissett had become a prime trade candidate in Arizona after being benched midgame against the Dallas Cowboys and then dropped to QB3 on the depth chart. He started the first eight games of the season for Arizona this season, going 3-5 with a 63.3% pass completion. After Brissett was benched during the loss to the Cowboys, the starting job was handed to Gardner Minshew, with Carson Beck the backup. West Palm Beach native Brissett will join his seventh NFL team in Baltimore, in his 11th season in the league. He was first selected by the New England Patriots in the third round of the 2016 Draft, going on to win the Super Bowl as Tom Brady's backup in his first season. He was traded to the Colts after his rookie season and was the starter there in 2017 and 2019, before alternating as a back-up and starter in Miami, Cleveland, Washington and back in New England, before eventually landing in Arizona. In March 2025 he signed a two-year, $12.5 million deal with the Cardinals and played in 14 games last season. Despite reworking his contract to increase his compensation for the 2026 season, he will become a free agent at the end of the campaign, unless he agrees new terms in Baltimore.

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Imagn Images It's safe to say that last week lived up to the hype. The Detroit Lions defeated the previously undefeated Minnesota Vikings , the Denver Broncos used a goal-line stand to hand Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs their second consecutive loss, and the Chicago Bears upset the Seahawks in Seattle with some help from trade-deadline addition Jeffery Simmons . This weekend in the NFL , the Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons will battle in Madrid, Jordan Love takes the Green Bay Packers to Foxborough to play the New England Patriots and Baker Mayfield gets a shot at Caleb Williams and the red-hot Bears. Which teams should you pick in Week 9, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 4 from DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research for its hard work. Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens (TNF) Dajani ( Jaguars -10): It's tough to pick this game since we are unaware of the Baltimore Ravens ' quarterback situation. Will they be starting rookie third-stringer Joe Fagnano , or someone else? I believe the Jaguars will win, but any team can cover a double-digit spread at home. Jacksonville is a remarkable 14-3 over its last 17 games and is the only NFL team leading its division by three or more games. Trevor Lawrence leads the NFL in passer rating (112.6), while the Jags lead the league in points per game differential (+12.1). Sure, you can say the Ravens will just ride Derrick Henry , but the Jaguars have what is statistically the No. 1 run defense in the NFL, and have gone 24 straight games without allowing a 75-yard rusher. … Prediction: Jaguars 28, Ravens 13 Dubin (Jaguars -10): The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. … Prediction: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) vs. Atlanta Falcons (Madrid) Dajani (Falcons +3): I may take the upset here. I'm aware the Falcons just registered one of the most embarrassing losses of the season in Tampa, but I'm willing to overlook that given how bad the weather was. I have some questions about the Bengals. Cornerback DJ Turner has a heel injury, and Cashius Howell just broke his wrist. Then, this Cincy defense allowed the lowly Tennessee Titans to put up 440 yards of total offense last week and allowed the first Titans' 300-yard passing game since the 2023 season. Tony Pollard rushed for 117 yards and two touchdowns, so what is Bijan Robinson going to do? Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the best wide receiving duo in the league, but the Bengals may be due for their first loss in over a month. Remember, this Falcons team beat the San Francisco 49ers the last time they played a game indoors. Give me the points. … Prediction: Falcons 27, Bengals 23 Dubin (Bengals -3): The Cincinnati offense is rolling, with Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins dunking on opposing defenses. Meanwhile, the Falcons have been struggling to run the ball as of late despite the presence of Bijan Robinson (48 carries for 200 scoreless yards in the last three weeks). The Bengals do provide an opportunity for the run game to get back on track (4.8 yards per carry allowed), but Dexter Lawrence has shut down other rushing attacks before. If the Bengals can keep Robinson in check, I'm not sure Atlanta can count on Michael Penix Jr . to go shot for shot with Burrow. … Prediction: Bengals 27, Falcons 20 Los Angeles Rams (-5.5) at Washington Commanders Dajani ( Rams -5.5): I think the Washington Commanders are a feisty team that could cover this number, but don't forget that this is somewhat of a revenge game for Sean McVay. He spent seven seasons in Washington before the Rams made the smart decision to hire this 30-year-old kid to run their franchise. In his first season as a head coach, McVay lost to his former team. Since then, he's 2-0 vs. Washington, winning each game by at least eight points. The Rams are coming off back-to-back wins by 14+ points. They also could get Myles Garrett back on Sunday. LA is 11-2 SU and 10-3 ATS in its last 13 games vs. teams entering below .500. … Prediction: Rams 27, Commanders 17 Dubin (Rams -5.5): The Rams have finally climbed back to .500 with back-to-back wins over the Raiders and Chargers , and I think they can keep things rolling here by doing what they did against those two teams: running the ball. Washington has actually been pretty good against the ground game this year, but it just lost Daron Payne to a significant injury. On the other side of the ball, I don't think we can count on the Commanders' offense to produce enough points to keep up with LA's offense. … Prediction: Rams 24, Commanders 16 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Dajani (Broncos -2.5): I told you the Broncos would beat the Chiefs last week. The conversation around Bo Nix is so bizarre to me. He's not Josh Allen , obviously, but he's not worth benching either. He's not the most prolific passer in NFL history, but he's Superman when it comes to leading his team to wins in crunch time. Denver does have a great defense, which pulled off that goal-line stand vs. Kansas City, but Nix leads the NFL since 2000 with 9.1 yards per attempt when down by one score in the fourth quarter. He has 15 game-winning drives to his name, which is one shy of the most in a three-season span in NFL history. Nix hasn't even played three full seasons. It hasn't always been pretty, but Nix is pretty good in those fourth quarters. This week, Denver travels to take on the Carolina Panthers . Bryce Young 's offensive line has some serious issues, and those were evident last week against the Packers. Through Week 8, Carolina has allowed 23 sacks, which is tied for second-most in the NFL, with 11 of those sacks coming in the past two games. Plus, the Panthers' defense has allowed an incredible 42.7 points per contest in their first three home games, which eventually led to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero last week. … Prediction: Broncos 24, Panthers 20 Dubin (Broncos -2.5): I'm not buying into Nix as much as Dajani is, but I am buying into Denver's defense being able to get after Bryce Young behind what is an increasingly leaky offensive line and preventing the Panthers from denting the scoreboard. If they can keep this a low-scoring game, I like them to pull out a win on the road. … Prediction: Broncos 23, Panthers 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (-3) Dajani (Packers +3): The Packers got some extra rest following their Thursday win over Carolina, while the New England Patriots couldn't run away from the Miami Dolphins . This Packers offense has been fun to watch — not counting the ground game, which has registered the fewest rushing yards (485) by a team above .500 through eight games in NFL history. However, Jordan Love leads the NFL with 2,246 passing yards, while Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are the first duo to have 600 yards receiving each through eight games since Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill in 2022! Drake Maye has been great, having scored at least three touchdowns over five straight games, but this Packers defense will provide quite the test. Green Bay has allowed just 14.6 points per game over its last five. … Prediction: Packers 27, Patriots 24 Dubin (Packers +3): I also think Green Bay's extra rest will matter here, even if only because it will give Christian Watson some extra time to heal up from the ribs injury he suffered last Thursday night. The Packers are going to need him against New England, even if he ends up drawing shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez , as that will just open things up for Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft . Meanwhile, Green Bay's defense has been excellent for several weeks now, and with the Patriots down multiple weapons in the passing game, I think the Packers can try to make New England one-dimensional here, limiting their chances to move the ball downfield. … Prediction: Packers 26, Patriots 20 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears (-6) (SNF) Dajani (Bears -6): I correctly chose Chicago to cover in Seattle last week, and I became even more confident in that pick when the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons. The Seahawks' addition of Quenton Nelson is a great one, but I think the addition of Simmons is even better. He's the best defensive tackle in the NFL and makes life incredibly difficult for quarterbacks. In his first game for his new team, he recorded six tackles, one sack and two tackles for loss. Chicago's defense allowed just 3.0 yards per play with him

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 9 picks, including the Bills handing the Vikings their second straight loss Imagn Images The turnaround week looked promising early Sunday. Then it went rotten — at least with my against-the-spread NFL picks , I went into the late games with a 6-3 ATS record. I ended up 7-7 for the week. That takes my season record to a horrible 50-68-3. As for my straight-up picks, I went 10-4. That brings my season record to 72-48-1. That I will take. Now it's time to get going on the ATS record. I went with some strange dogs this week in hopes of getting back on track. Let's hope they bark. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Jaguars get a break on a short week, not having to face Lamar Jackson at quarterback. The Ravens are a different team without him and now must play rookie Joe Fagnano . Trevor Lawrence is playing at a high level and the run game is going well. Look for the Jaguars to win a road game on a short week. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 16 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Madrid on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals have been flying high on offense with Joe Burrow throwing it around. The Falcons have struggled on offense in recent weeks, which is never a good thing when trying to keep up with Burrow. Look for a lot more big plays from the Bengals as they win this one in Spain. Pick: Bengals 33, Falcons 21 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Panthers have been beat up the past two games, leading to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. They are reeling on defense. The Broncos won a tough one last week against the Chiefs thanks to late-game magic by Bo Nix . This time, it's a lot easier against a bad Panthers defense and struggling offensive line. Pick: Broncos 26, Panthers 20 Dallas Cowboys (-6) at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys are coming off a horrible loss to the Cardinals at home, but they get a big break playing the Colts , who are struggling. Indianapolis has major problems and there is talk of trading more players. The Cowboys will get the offense cranked up again in this one as they get back on track behind their passing game. Pick: Cowboys 31, Colts 17 New York Jets (+9.5) at Kansas City Chiefs The Chiefs are back home after losing two straight on the road. The Jets blew a late lead to the Raiders last week. Kansas City has not run it the past two weeks, but look for Kenneth Walker to get back on track. The Chiefs win it to break the losing streak, but the Jets and their offense hang around. Pick: Chiefs 24, Jets 17 Detroit Lions (-7) at Miami Dolphins This is a tough trip for the Lions coming off two home division victories, and it's against a young team playing much better. But this is a big challenge for the Miami defense. The Lions can score in bunches and I think they will in this one. Look for a big day from Jared Goff . Pick: Lions 30, Dolphins 13 Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints (-1.5) The Browns are playing consecutive road games after losing to the Steelers last week. The Saints are coming off a bye, so big advantage there. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game. Pick: Saints 17, Browns 14 New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles (+3.5) The Giants are coming off a bye in first place in the division, while the Eagles are coming off a road loss Sunday night to the Commanders . They are struggling in many areas. But this is a big rivalry, and pride will help keep the Eagles in it, as their defense has a solid day against J.J. McCarthy . But the Giants win it late. Pick: Giants 22, Eagles 20 Los Angeles Rams at Washington Commanders (+5.5) This is a long trip for the Rams , but they seemed to have righted things the past few weeks. The Commanders rallied to beat the Eagles Sunday night. The Washington defense played well in that game, but this could be a game where Matt Stafford gets it cranked up. Jayden Daniels will play well to keep it close, but the Rams will win it. Pick: Rams 28, Commanders 24 Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Texans are coming off a bye, while the Chargers are coming off a loss to the Rams. Neither team has come close to expectations before the season, with the Chargers winless. The Texans' defense and the Chargers' offense have both struggled. But I think the Chargers will hang around in this one behind their defense. Pick: Texans 19, Chargers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at San Francisco 49ers (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, while the 49ers are coming off a bye. Big edge for the 49ers. Plus, they are the better team. The Raiders' defense is struggling, so look for Brock Purdy to have a big day throwing the football. 49ers big. Pick: 49ers 31, Raiders 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (+3.5) This has the feel of a low-scoring game with two good defenses — even though both teams have good quarterbacks. The Packers have added rest from playing last Thursday, which will help. The Patriots had to rally and beat the Dolphins last week. The defenses play well, but It's Jordan Love who makes the plays late to win it. Pick: Packers 19, Patriots 16 Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks (-12.5) The Seahawks are coming off an embarrassing home loss to the Bears , while the Cardinals won at Dallas last week. They are making a quarterback change to Gardner Minshew , who played well last week. Good luck against this Seattle defense, which will be hunting after the Bears beat them. The Cardinals will get the brunt of their anger. Pick: Seahawks 30, Cardinals 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are coming off that impressive victory over Seattle Monday night on the road. That was domination. But there might be a little letdown here. The Bucs have played impressive defense this season and have cranked up their running game. They will run it well here, but in the end, Caleb Williams will make late plays to win it. Pick: Bears 24, Bucs 21 Buffalo Bills (-3.5) at Minnesota Vikings Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the game of the week, featuring two of the better teams in the league. I can't wait to see the Vikings ' defense against Josh Allen . But I think the Bills will run the ball at the Minnesota defense, much like the Lions did last week. The Bills defense has been better as of late, and that will show up against a limited Minnesota offense. My Bengals vs. Falcons prediction has Cincinnati packing extra luggage to carry its momentum to Madrid, where the Bengals look to extend their winning ways against Atlanta on Sunday morning. Cincinnati is laying just over a field goal inside Santiago Bernabéu Stadium and is riding a three-game streak into Week 9, though it built that run against some softer opposition. Read on for the edges in this international encounter and my best NFL picks to wake up to on Sunday, Nov. 8, starring Tee Higgins. Bengals vs Falcons prediction: Falcons +3.5 The Cincinnati Bengals are rolling right now, but those victories have come against some weaker opponents. They took down bottom-feeders like Miami and Tennessee (barely), while needing a second-half rally to overcome Baltimore and a backup QB. There was also a bye in Week 6 giving Cincy a breather. I believe the Bengals should be the favorites in Spain, but not by this many points. The Atlanta Falcons are coming off a strange Week 8 loss in which weather played a huge role in the result. That included four interceptions from QB Michael Penix Jr. , who had only one INT in the previous five starts. I'm not discounting Atlanta too much for that rain-soaked squash at Tampa Bay. Rather, I see the Falcons facing one of the easier defenses on their recent schedule, with the Bengals stop unit slipping the past three games. The most notable dip has come defending the run. The Bengals are allowing 5.1 yards per carry in their last three outings (second most in the NFL). Not what you want to see when staring down Bijan Robinson . Bengals vs Falcons combo The Bengals should be favorites, but their current three-game win streak is very puffed up, and Atlanta poses a stiffer test on a neutral field. I'll take Atlanta on the other side of a field goal. Chase Brown hasn't found paydirt since Week 1. The Falcons have given up 11 total touchdowns to running backs and Brown is a dual-threat option, either running it past the goal line or catching a TD strike. Tee Higgins could be the best WR2 in the league. He's the top-rated WR versus man coverage and faces plenty of one-on-one coverage from Atlanta. Projections call for another big day, with most models north of 80 yards receiving from Higgins. Chase Brown touchdown Tee Higgins 75+ receiving yards TOP PICK Bengals vs Falcons player prop: Tee Higgins 75+ receiving yards Bengals receiver Tee Higgins is coming off a monster day versus Tennessee, drawing 11 targets for 10 catches and 155 yards. Higgins could be the best WR2 in the league, with Ja'Marr Chase drawing the ire of the secondary and leaving the 6-foot-4 Higgins with softer matchups. He gets a perfect pairing against Atlanta in Madrid. The Falcons rank 24th in DVOA defending WR2s , allowing an average of 54.6 yards per game to the position. This secondary is also running a high rate of man coverage (10th most), and Higgins currently rates as the No. 1 WR versus man at PFF. Projections for Higgins range from 74 to 88 yards on Sunday morning, with most models north of 80 yards. My number comes out to 81.5 receiving yards in Madrid. Want more NFL player props? Cincinnati and Atlanta will do battle in Spain in a game that could deliver plenty of fireworks for fans. The NFL sent two incredible offensive teams to Madrid that could put up plenty of points. After all, exciting games like this one can really expand the league's footprint on the international stage. Both teams have quite a lot in common. They are both in extremely tight division races where just one win could propel them into first place. However, the difference between the AFC North and the NFC South is absolutely massive. Still, the Falcons have looked impressive at times throughout the season. Meanwhile, the Bengals have been fairly consistent now that their defense is finally looking solid. Though they did not look good against the Titans last week. Regardless, both teams are hungry for a win and have all the offensive weapons needed to get it done. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So which team will come out on top in this one? And will this game become an offensive shootout or a defensive struggle? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this huge international clash between the Bengals and Falcons in Madrid. Joe Burrow has a repeat of his Week 8 offensive explosion against the Falcons Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports The Bengals looked like a vintage version of the team in Week 8 against the Dolphins. Yes, Cincinnati did get the win. But it was shocking how much they needed to lean on Burrow to get the job done. Fortunately, Burrow is one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL and passed that tough test with flying colors. Burrow finished 38-of-48 for 462 passing yards with five touchdowns and three interceptions. He also had one rushing touchdown. The veteran quarterback simply put the team on his back and willed them to victory. Now Burrow and friends must face an average Falcons defense that's allowed 223.4 passing yards per game this season. Keep in mind that the best opponent Atlanta has faced this season is Chicago. In that game, Caleb Williams shredded their secondary for 305 passing yards. Beyond that game, the Falcons have not been tested very much through the air this season. So just how much damage could Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins do against the Falcons? Burrow will have a repeat performance from last week, going over 400 passing yards and throwing at least three touchdown passes. Cincinnati has to throw the ball to win right now, so they'll be comfortable going guns blazing. To make this even bolder, both Higgins and Chase will each go over 100 receiving yards and score a touchdown. Bijan Robinson will have twice as many rushing yards as the Bengals The disparity between Atlanta and Cincinnati's running game is absolutely massive. Cincinnati has one of the worst rushing attacks in the entire league. In fact, they only average 80.3 rushing yards per game so far this season. That average is quite concerning since they've already played in seven games, so a few bad performances aren't dragging it down. Chase Brown and company just aren't getting the job done. Atlanta is the exact opposite, with their Bijan Robinson-led rushing attack as one of the best in the NFL. They've averaged 134.8 rushing yards per game this year. Only the Buccaneers, Bears, and Bills have a better average. Robinson is the main reason why the Falcons have such a huge advantage on the ground. Just how good will he do in comparison to the Bengals in Madrid? Bijan is averaging 100.6 rushing yards per game in 2026. He is single-handedly outperforming the Bengals on the ground despite failing to break 100 rushing yards in four consecutive games. The Falcons know that they need Robinson to pop off if they want a chance to win this game. They'll design a game plan to do exactly that, and it has a great chance to work. Bijan won't just have more rushing yards than the Bengals, he'll double them up. All it would take is an elite game by Robinson and a pass-happy attack from Cincinnati's offense. Falcons, Bengals combine for at least 80 points in an exciting shootout in Madrid Image Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images This game has all the necessary ingredients of an offensive shootout. Burrow and friends should have no problem scoring at will in this game. Bijan and the Falcons have a huge advantage running the ball. That should keep their offense consistent throughout this game, even if the Bengals start running up the score. Make no mistake, the Bengals have a solid defense that is both frisky and opportunistic. They won't be playing to their strengths when going up against Bijan on the ground. But once the offense gets established, Cincinnati could start to pull away. They should come away with the victory as long as nothing too fluky happens. The Bengals will come out on top thanks to their high-powered offense than can score at the drop of a hat. If they need points late in this game, they will make it happen. The same is not true for the Falcons. Related: NFL picks, predictions, odds for Week 9: Can home dogs bite? Related: NFL Fantasy Football Week 9 2026 Start 'Em Sit 'Em: D/ST

(Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kevin Knight · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 4:34 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Falcons squandered a golden opportunity to take control of the NFC South in Week 8, falling completely flat in a bad weather game against the Bucs. Now sitting at 3-5—along with the rest of the division—Atlanta is in a difficult place. Games against some of the AFC and NFC's best await over the next month, sandwiched around the team's Week 11 bye. The first game in this sequence comes early Sunday morning in Madrid, as the Falcons take on the Bengals. Cincinnati is a bit volatile, but possesses one of the best offenses in the NFL led by quarterback Joe Burrow and the elite receiver duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Right now, the Falcons are 3-point underdogs against the Bengals, per FanDuel. Atlanta needs a victory to stay afloat in the playoff hunt, but can it come against this Cincinnati team? Let's take a closer look. Falcons vs Bengals Week 9 predictions The Bengals hold the NFL's second-best scoring offense, best third-down offense, and are also top-10 in total yardage. This will be one of the biggest tests for Atlanta's defense all season. The good news for the Falcons is that Cincinnati's offense is very one-dimensional, with the vast majority of their production coming via the passing game. Over the past few weeks, Atlanta's biggest issue has been stopping the run. That shouldn't be a problem in Week 9, as the Bengals are 30th in rushing yardage and 28th in yards per carry. So all eyes then turn to the Falcons ability to slow down Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. I'm not sure how well the Falcons will fare, but having their full complement of cornerbacks available will be a big help. A.J. Terrell, C.J. Henderson, and Billy Bowman are back in the lineup together for the first time since September. Joe Burrow has been fantastic, but he's still vulnerable to pressure. With the Falcons (hopefully) getting star edge rusher James Pearce Jr. back in the lineup this weekend, the pass rush is the best path to victory. Atlanta has been outstanding generating interior pressure and pretty solid outside, but has lacked a true finisher to pile up sacks. Pearce brings that ability, and will hopefully bring a big boost to the defensive line on passing downs. On the other side of the ball, the message is simple: the Falcons offense must get back on track, and can't afford to start slow. Michael Penix Jr. is coming off a career-worst performance in a monsoon against the Bucs. The Bengals defense has been opportunistic and good at limiting scoring, but gives up a ton of yardage. This will be the softest defense the Falcons have faced in weeks, and they must take advantage. Atlanta will need a good day from Penix and the passing game to keep pace with Burrow, but the biggest player to watch is probably Bijan Robinson. This game has the potential to be a "Bijan takeover" performance, with Cincinnati 29th in yards per carry allowed on defense. Bijan got a bit stuck in the mud against Tampa Bay, and I think he'll have an explosive game in Madrid. All in all, it likely comes down to the Falcons ability to limit the Bengals offensive chances by holding the ball as much as possible, and capitalizing on their own scoring opportunities. Cincinnati is beatable—the game last week against the Titans showed that—but you have to be able to keep up with them offensively. home.headline: Falcons Suddenly Rule Out Running Back Ahead of Bengals Matchup in Spain
home.blurb: Falcons Suddenly Rule Out Running Back Ahead of Bengals Matchup in Spain Falcons Rule Out Running Back vs Bengals After listing him as questionable entering Friday morning, the Falcons have officially changed their injury report and ruled out running back Brian Robinson Jr. for Sunday's game with a hamstring injury. This will mark his third consecutive game on the sidelines. Via ESPN's Adam Schefter : “F alcons ruled out RB Brian Robinson Jr . for Sunday’s game in Madrid against the Bengals due to a hamstring injury.” Falcons ruled out RB Brian Robinson Jr. for Sunday’s game in Madrid against the Bengals due to a hamstring injury. https://t.co/NDIAdtS66M However, he was traded to the San Francisco 49ers in 2025, where he saw limited carries behind Christian McCaffrey. He's now taken on a similar role in Atlanta. Unlock the latest Heavy on Bengals news — direct to your inbox. The Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons are in Madrid, Spain, for what should be a memorable international showdown on Sunday. Ahead of the matchup, which will kick off at 9:30 a.m. ET for viewers in the United States, the Falcons made a sudden change to their injury report. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 6, 2026 Robinson Jr. has played an important role in the Falcons' offense this season, often giving starter Bijan Robinson Jr. a break and taking some of the workload off his shoulders. Without Robinson Jr. over the last two games, Atlanta's other running backs, primarily Khalil Herbert, have produced little to nothing. Robinson Jr.'s 2026 Season With Falcons Robinson Jr. is in his fifth NFL season and first with the Falcons. He has played in six games this year. He has rushed 53 times for 211 yards and four touchdowns, averaging 4.0 yards per carry. That's solid production for a backup running back who rarely gets opportunities because Bijan handles most of the workload. Robinson Jr. spent the first three years of his career with the Washington Commanders after a stellar collegiate career at Alabama. At one point, he appeared poised to become Washington's featured running back. home.headline: Ja’Marr Chase Injury Update Reveals Bengals WR’s Status Before Falcons Matchup
home.blurb: For fantasy managers, the evidence supports treating Chase as available, and the Week 9 slate offers little reason to sit him. The final inactive report remains the last confirmation before kickoff, and no verified report currently suggests a restriction. The bigger problem sits with Atlanta. Higgins is coming off a 155-yard afternoon, and Chase just produced 141 yards of his own. Burrow has thrown 20 touchdowns through seven games. If the full group is available Sunday, the Falcons have to defend a passing attack that spreads the ball without moving away from its top receiver. Ja'Marr Chase Injury Update Reveals Bengals WR's Status Before Falcons Matchup By Nishat | November 4, 2026 | Featured , NFL Ja'Marr Chase enters Week 9 in Madrid off the best receiving afternoon of his season. He caught 11 passes for 141 yards in the Cincinnati Bengals ‘ 43-36 overtime win over the Tennessee Titans , and he found the end zone in that same game. The only open question was whether the short turnaround to Spain changed anything. Cincinnati's latest injury report answered it. Chase is not listed on the Week 9 injury report. Ja'Marr Chase Injury Update Gives Bengals WR Clear Status The Bengals left Chase off their Wednesday report entirely. That report was only an estimate because the team held a walkthrough instead of a full practice, but it did not carry any new designation for the club's top receiver. Chase also made the trip. He traveled with the team to Madrid on Tuesday, and Bengals.com published a travel photo identifying him among the players on board ahead of the league's international weekend against the Atlanta Falcons . That leaves no verified reason to describe Chase as injured. The report instead points toward normal availability, though the inactive list will not be final until game day. The Week 8 outing was his strongest of the season. Chase caught 11 of 16 targets for 141 yards against the Titans, with a 30-yard long and one trip to the end zone. His 16 targets were a season high. The performance pushed his 2026 totals to 43 catches for 492 yards, and he has six touchdowns through seven games, according to NFL statistics. Joe Burrow played one of his strongest games of the season as well. He completed 38 of 48 passes for 462 yards against Tennessee. He threw five passing touchdowns in that game and added a rushing score. That connection gives Cincinnati every reason to involve Chase early against Atlanta. The Falcons have to account for him while also handling Tee Higgins . Bengals Still Have Another Major Target Tee Higgins arrives in Week 9 as the AFC Offensive Player of the Week. He caught 10 passes for 155 yards against Tennessee and scored twice. Through 7 games, he has 43 catches for 726 yards. His 16.9 yards per catch led the Bengals among their main receivers. home.headline: Falcons Week 9 injury report: Latest on James Pearce, Divine Deablo
home.blurb: "Asked about Pearce, Stefanski said the Falcons are pleased with where he is in terms of being football ready," wrote team reporter Tori McElhaney . "He's been working out with the Falcons strength staff for the last month, per his suspension rules. That said, Stefanski added the Falcons will use the rest of this week to determine how many snaps Pearce gets this Sunday against the Cincinnati Bengals." Wide receiver Zachariah Branch sat out as expected with a hamstring injury. Stefanski has already ruled the rookie return man out for Sunday's game. Branch was the only player to log a "DNP" on Wednesday, though. Linebacker Divine Deablo, running back Brian Robinson Jr. and LB Yasir Abdullah (designated to return from IR) were limited participants to begin Week 9. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. was a full participant. Check out the full Falcons-Bengals injury report below. WR Zachariah Branch (hamstring): DNP/OUT RB Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring): LP/OUT The Atlanta Falcons have arrived in Madrid, Spain for their Week 9 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals . The team held a brief walkthrough on Wednesday morning and released a simulated injury report shortly after. Edge rusher James Pearce Jr. was listed as a full participant for the first time all season. Pearce, who was suspended for the first eight games for his violation of the NFL's personal conduct policy, is expected to make his 2026 debut this Sunday against the Bengals. The Defensive Rookie of the Year finalist led all rookies in sacks with 10.5 last season. Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said Pearce was in good shape and that the team would monitor him this week to determine how much the second-year edge rusher would play against Cincinnati. home.headline: Is Baker Mayfield Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Falcons vs. Buccaneers in NFL Week 8)
home.blurb: Is Baker Mayfield Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Falcons vs. Buccaneers in NFL Week 8) Skip to main content ON SI Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield returned from a three-game absence due to a dislocated thumb in Week 7, and he's off the team's injury report and expected to play in Week 8. Mayfield guided the Bucs to their second win of the season against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7, and oddsmakers are buying the Buccaneers at home in Week 8 against the Atlanta Falcons. The Buccaneers are favored to win their matchup with the Falcons, sitting as 2.5-point favorites in the odds at DraftKings Sportsbook . After a 1-5 start to the season, Tampa Bay's win over Carolina thrust it back into the mix to win the division this season. Another win over an NFC South opponent would go a long way for Tampa Bay getting into the playoffs, and the running game has really stepped forward in recent weeks with both Mayfield and Jalon Daniels under center. Mayfield wasn't asked to do much against Carolina, completing just seven of his 11 passes for 76 yards and a score. He's completed 63.6 percent of his passes for 679 yards, three scores and two picks in four games. Daniels led Tampa Bay to one win while Mayfield was sidelined, but it's pretty clear that oddsmakers view the former No. 1 overall pick as a major upgrade under center. Mayfield and the Bucs take on Altanta and Chicago over the next two weeks before their bye. Atlanta is currently one game ahead of Tampa Bay in the NFC South, but a win on Sunday would vault the Bucs into second in the divison, just a half-game back of the Panthers (3-4). away.blurb: Sunday’s matchup at Lucas Oil Stadium brings together two teams badly in need of a reset, as the Dallas Cowboys (3-5) visit the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) at 1 p.m. ET. Dallas is coming off a crushing 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in which it led 24-10 early in the fourth quarter and 30-24 in the final minute, only for Gardner Minshew to lead an 80-yard game-tying touchdown drive before Chad Ryland won it with a 42-yard field goal in overtime. Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown and added a five-yard rushing score, but Dallas managed only 261 total yards and went three-and-out on its lone overtime possession. The loss dropped the Cowboys to 3-5 and magnified a season-long problem: the defense. Dallas is allowing 26.6 points and 385.4 yards per game. The most recent meeting between these teams produced one of the wildest quarters in Cowboys’ history. On December 4, 2022, Indianapolis trailed 21-19 entering the fourth quarter in Arlington before Dallas erupted for 33 unanswered points to win 54-19. Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Tony Pollard ran for 91 yards and two scores, and the Cowboys forced five turnovers, including Malik Hooker’s 38-yard fumble-return touchdown against his former team. The recent series has otherwise gone back and forth: Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0 in 2018, Dallas won 42-7 in 2014, the Cowboys earned a 38-35 overtime victory in 2010, and Dallas won 21-14 in 2006. What if Brad Holmes could bring a former Minnesota Vikings starting safety to Detroit? Cam Bynum , now with the Indianapolis Colts, has been identified as a potential trade target for the Lions. The 28-year-old defensive back has extensive starting experience, a history of making plays against the pass, and the versatility to potentially help a Detroit defense that has been dealing with injuries. But there is one major obstacle that could make a deal difficult. Former Vikings Safety Emerges as Lions Trade Idea In a November 6 examination of 17 possible Lions trade targets , NFL analyst Jeff Risdon identified Bynum as an intriguing option for general manager Brad Holmes. Risdon suggested Indianapolis could consider moving the veteran as the Colts evaluate their roster. He also pointed to Bynum’s ability to provide more range in deep coverage than current Detroit safety Chuck Clark. The Lions have needed dependable play on the back end of their defense throughout the season, and Bynum has experience handling precisely that responsibility. During his four seasons with Minnesota, Bynum developed into a reliable starter capable of playing deep safety, supporting the run, and creating turnovers. He started all 17 games in three consecutive seasons from 2022 through 2024, showing the kind of availability Detroit could certainly appreciate. However, this is a hypothetical trade idea. There is no confirmed report that the Lions have contacted Indianapolis about Bynum or that the Colts have placed him on the trade block. home.blurb: The Dallas Cowboys are running out of healthy bodies in the secondary with the Indianapolis Colts coming to town. And a key defender popped up on the injury report out of nowhere. When Porter Jr. was a participant on Wednesday, those concerns eased a bit. On Thursday, however, the Cowboys listed him as a limited participant again. Speaking of the secondary, safeties Caleb Downs and PJ Locke remain in the concussion protocol. Each was upgraded from a non-participant on Wednesday to a limited participant on Thursday. NFL players who enter the protocol often miss at least one week, but there's no set minimum number of days a player has to sit. In 2023, CBS Sports insider Jonathan Jones reported that the median return from a concussion is nine days. At least Downs and Locke took a significant step forward by getting back to on-field activity as limited participants. Sticking with the defense, linebacker DeMarvion Overshown is a new addition to the report. He wasn't listed on Wednesday, but he was limited on Thursday with a hamstring/back injury. Overshown didn't play from Week 1 against the New York Giants until he returned against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7. Seeing him back on the injury report isn't encouraging. It doesn't necessarily mean he'll be out on Sunday. As for the rest of the linebacker group, Dee Winters continues to trend in the right direction. He was upgraded to a full participant on Thursday’s practice and is in line to return to the active roster. Wide receiver George Pickens remains on the report after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday. He's now listed with only a hamstring injury, not a shoulder injury. At tight end, Luke Schoonmaker was limited again on Thursday. He missed the last game against the Cardinals with a groin injury, and his status for Week 9 might matter more than expected. Jake Ferguson missed his second straight practice of the week after getting hurt early against Arizona. Elsewhere, edge rusher Malachi Lawrence and returner KaVontae Turpin were non-participants. Offensive tackle Tyler Smith was limited on both Wednesday and Thursday with an ankle injury, but the Cowboys didn't appear concerned about his availability for Week 9. Last week the Jets lost at home against the previously winless Miami Dolphins. This week the Las Vegas Raiders broke their own four game losing streak by out-scoring the Jets in a wild 38 – 33 shootout in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Jets took a nine point lead into the locker room at halftime, only to unravel in the second half. The Jets defense was helpless to stop the Raiders attack in the second half as the Jets were out-scored 24 – 10 to close the game. It was a humiliating performance by a putrid Jets defense. The embarrassing Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-6 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Any hopes of a playoff run are all but gone. The Chiefs opened the 2026 season with a dominant 31 – 10 victory over the Denver Broncos. They followed that impressive win with four straight victories over some of the worst teams in the NFL – the Indianapolis Colts, Miami Dolphins, Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Chargers. The 5-0 start to the season was great, but with four of the wins coming against bad teams, it is tough to say just how good the Chiefs are. Now they have lost two straight to tough opponents. Are the Chiefs a top team? Maybe. It's not entirely clear. What is crystal clear is the Chiefs are a far, far better team than the Jets. Teams like the Dolphins and the Raiders have snapped their losing streaks against the Jets in East Rutherford. It seems all but inevitable Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs will do the same at home. away.headline: Jets announce concerning injury update on WR Garrett Wilson
away.blurb: The New York Jets could be without their No. 1 wide receiver weapon in Sunday’s Week 9 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. When speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn announced that Garrett Wilson is in the NFL ‘s concussion protocol and considered “day-to-day” moving forward. “Garrett, he’s in the concussion protocol. He’ll be day-to-day,” Glenn said. Wilson, who’s been openly frustrated about his role in the Jets’ offense so far this season, had six catches for 83 yards in this past Sunday’s 38-33 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders. Wilson’s practice status later this week will be a good indication of his potential availability for Sunday’s road matchup against the Chiefs. Fortunately for the Jets, wide receiver Adonai Mitchell is back from injury and performing at a high level. In Sunday’s loss to the Raiders, he paced New York with seven catches for 142 yards and a touchdown. Rookie pass catcher Omar Cooper Jr. has also flashed brilliance on a few occasions in his debut campaign. Sunday’s Week 9 matchup against the Chiefs will kick off at 1 p.m. ET from Arrowhead Stadium. away.headline: New York Jets Edge David Bailey Back to Full Practice, Will Face Kansas City Chiefs
away.blurb: The Jets did receive some good injury news. Edge David Bailey, who sat out the Raiders game with a groin injury sustained against Miami, has returned to full practice. Getting pressure on Mahomes will be key to any Jets hopes of victory, so Bailey’s comeback is a big key to the team’s schemes. Also likely out for the Jets is reserve linebacker Trevin Wallace, who also didn’t practice on Thursday. Perennial injured list occupant and Jets edge Joseph Ossai was listed as limited in practice as he continues nursing an ankle injury. The Jets earlier announced that star receiver Garrett Wilson would not be available for the Kansas City game. Wilson is in the NFL concussion protocol from a blow to the head sustained on the next-to-last play of the Las Vegas Raiders game. He is likely week-to-week before he returns. The defensive wall is crumbling for the New York Jets. They’ve now given up 28 or more points in two straight games, and their interior defense is being devastated by injuries. Defensive tackle Harrison Phillips missed practice again on Thursday with an ankle injury. The Jets have already lost man-mountain T’Vondre Sweat to injured reserve, leaving the team without two of their interior stalwarts against the run. The Jets now head to Kansas City to face Chiefs’ perennial All-pro Patrick Mahomes and running back Kenneth Walker, the latter third in the NFL in rushing yards. It could be a long day if Jets like defensive linemen Darrell Jackson Jr. don’t step up. In one last hopeful sign, running back Breece Hall is expected to play Sunday. It would be his first game back after missing five straight contests with a quad muscle injury.

Led by first-year head coach Jeff Hafley, the Dolphins have struggled to do much right in 2026. Through seven games, they've scored the second-fewest points (16.7/contest), plus they've allowed the ninth-most points (25.9/game). Additionally, Miami did not notch its first win of the season until Week 7, defeating Aaron Glenn and the N.Y. Jets, 28-25. Undeniably, it's been a rough season for Hafley & Co., which find themselves in possession of the third-worst record in the NFL. The only teams which have been worse are the Tennessee Titans (1-7) and the L.A. Chargers (0-7). The Lions, under Dan Campbell, were once in the same unenviable shoes as the Dolphins. When Campbell first took over in the Motor City in 2021, Detroit was far from one of the most formidable teams in the NFL. Instead, just like the Dolphins currently, Campbell & Co. experienced their fair share of struggles and lost plenty of games on their way to establishing their tough, gritty identity. In fact, Detroit started the aforementioned campaign 0-10-1 before winning its first game in Week 13 against the Minnesota Vikings. In that sense, Campbell sees plenty of parallels between those Lions and this current iteration of Miami. “Coach Hafley’s done a good job in his first year,” the sixth-year Lions head man expressed to reporters this week. “A lot of similarities — it reminds me of what we were when we came in. They’re young, they’re hungry, they’re active, they run, they hit, they hustle, they finish, try to play disciplined ball. And they’re playing that way.” As much as Campbell's squad is undoubtedly the better team, you can't take anyone lightly in the NFL. And for as bad as the Dolphins have been, it's important to note they have not lost a game by more than seven points since Week 4. Their last double-digit loss came in Week 3 against the Kansas City Chiefs (24-10). And on top of all that, the Lions are severely banged up entering this Week 9 matchup , after suffering a plethora of injuries a week ago against Minnesota. They lost five total defensive players in the divisional tilt, including defensive captain Jack Campbell, the two best members of their secondary (Brian Branch and D.J. Reed) and EDGE DJ Wonnum. And they all are in danger of missing Detroit’s interconference contest in Miami. As a result, Miami – led under center by fifth-year passer Malik Willis – might have a chance to do some damage against Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit . Yet, the Lions are seven-point favorites, per multiple sportsbooks, for a reason, and should emerge victorious in the road affair. At this present juncture, I'll give Detroit a 72 percent chance to secure the Week 9 victory . While the Lions are shaking off some early-season mistakes, they've strung together three wins, including back-to-back wins in their division, while the Dolphins are in the early stages of a rebuild under their latest regime. The folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -7 points . The Dolphins made a general manager and head coaching change this offseason, firing GM Chris Grier and coach Mike McDaniel after four unsuccessful seasons and hiring Jon-Eric Sullivan as their new GM and former Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley as their new coach. Like most new regimes, the new staff got to work early, cutting veteran contracts, including quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and edge rusher Bradley Chubb. They also traded away former first-round pick Jaylen Waddle for a trio of picks to use in the 2026 NFL Draft to help them with the rebuild. Step one in establishing a new foundation was signing Malik Willis as their new signal caller—who most recently played in Green Bay with Hafley—and drafting six (!) rookie starters, including first-round picks guard Kadyn Proctor and corner Chris Johnson, as well as second-round pick linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, third-round receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, and fifth-round safety Michael Taaffe. They also have another eight rookies on their 53-man roster, meaning over 25% of the Dolphins roster (14 players) is made up of first-year players. As you would expect with a young roster at the beginning of a rebuild, the Dolphins have struggled out of the gate. In Week 1, the Raiders beat them by two touchdowns; the 49ers won by three touchdowns the week after; and the Chiefs beat them by two touchdowns in Week 3. In Week 4, they showed signs of improvement, losing to the Vikings by only five points; the Bengals won by just seven in Week 5, and in Week 6, they got their first win of the season, beating the Jets by three points. On Sunday, the Dolphins and Patriots squared off in an AFC East showdown, and while the Dolphins built a 13-3 lead at the half, the Patriots scored 21 unanswered points to go up 24-13 late in the fourth quarter. Willis connected on an explosive touchdown pass at the 2-minute warning to bring them close, but a failed 2-point conversion and a failed onside kick set the final score at 24-19. We learned about the local sentiment surrounding head coach Jeff Hafley's foundational reset, how offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik is tailoring the offense to quarterback Malik Willis, and how Ollie Gordon is handling the backfield workload in De'Von Achane's absence—plus what Miami needs to do to keep pace with Detroit's offense. 1. Miami arguably made more changes to their organization than any other team in the NFL this offseason. New head coach, new quarterback, the changing out of long-tenured skill position players—it was a massive overhaul in South Beach. Although the Dolphins are off to a 1-6 start, how much of that was expected from a team that underwent so many changes this offseason? It's early, but do you get the sense that new head coach Jeff Hafley is the right guy for this rebuild? This year is about setting up the franchise for the future, and while losses are never fun, the struggles were expected. This is the league's youngest team, and they are facing a steep learning curve. Miami has 14 rookies on the roster, plus another seven first-year players. This is clearly a reset of the team's foundation, and there will be growing pains. The Dolphins' schedule has also been brutal this year. They started the year against the Las Vegas Raiders, San Francisco 49ers, Kansas City Chiefs, and Minnesota Vikings, not facing a team that had a loss until Week 5 against the Cincinnati Bengals, who were 2-2 coming into that game. Through Week 8, Miami has faced the league's toughest schedule, with a combined opponent winning percentage of .589. The schedule is not an excuse, but with such a young team, it is another variable to consider. Obviously, things can change, but Hafley has instilled confidence in the fanbase so far. The Mike McDaniel era had some fun moments, but it quickly fell apart and the team never adjusted (and McDaniel still does not seem to have made adjustments as the Los Angeles Chargers struggle this year). I think Hafley's focus on making the Dolphins physical, allowing the younger players to gain experience, and the team's ability to make adjustments, learn from mistakes, and continue to fight even in losing situations indicate he is the right guy for this role. Lions fans saw Dan Campbell build a culture out of tough losses back in 2021; that is exactly the phase Hafley and the Dolphins are in right now. 2. From the outside looking in, Malik Willis was dropped into a tough situation given the pieces around him in the offense—and it looks like, predictably, the passing game has struggled so far. The Dolphins rank 26th in passing DVOA and EPA/pass. How has Bobby Slowik tried to tailor this offense to Willis' strengths? What's working, what's not working, and how much of that is related to a new quarterback in a new system versus the lack of talent personnel-wise? I think we are starting to see Willis find some comfort in the offensive system, and he is starting to play better. Despite being a third-round pick in 2022, Willis has played in only 29 career games, starting just 13. He is a league veteran but really has the starting experience of a rookie. At times, he still seems bothered by the speed of the game, but the experience he is getting this year is already making a difference in his play. I think one of the biggest issues we have seen from Willis is a desire to be a pocket passer. He stays in the pocket longer than he should, trying to find the perfect pass rather than taking something shorter or throwing the ball away to avoid a sack. The offensive line is not doing him any favors, but he has taken multiple sacks by running out of bounds instead of throwing the ball away. He seemed to want to avoid using his legs, but has opened up that part of his game in the last couple of weeks. Slowik, like McDaniel before him, has an offensive system built on quarterback accuracy and timing. He uses bootlegs, run-pass options, and play-action passes to get Willis out of the pocket and seeing open receivers. They also seem to be using some half-field concepts, keeping Willis looking in one area and working from deep to shallow rather than having him search the entire field for receivers. The youth on the roster – especially with wide receivers Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell, and Kevin Coleman Jr. – do not always create separation, and drops have also been an issue. When the primary target is not open on time, a young quarterback hesitates, and behind an evolving offensive line, hesitation leads to sacks. That all relates back to the discussion of Miami's reset this year. The potential for talent is on Miami's roster, but they still need to grow individually and together. The coaching staff is clearly working on the balance between youth and system – relying on a more basic system as the players learn. 3. Losing De'Von Achane in the first month of the season felt especially cruel for this offense that was already so limited on difference makers. The Dolphins rank 9th in EPA/rush (-0.03) but rank near the bottom of the league in rush success rate (26th) and rush DVOA (26th), suggesting that their run game is a boom-or-bust attack. Is that a fair assessment of Ollie Gordon's performance this year? The Dolphins also rank 26th in stuffed rate (22.8%) which is the percentage of runs that earn zero or negative yards. Are those stuffed runs more of an indictment of the offensive line or the coaching/play calling? That seems like a fair assessment. Gordon has been a lot of fun to watch as he breaks out this year, but he is a power-back who works extremely well as a change-of-pace option behind Achane. When he finds space, he is able to break it for a big gain, but it really is boom or bust on each run. Part of that is Gordon and his abilities. Part of that is the offensive line finding space to get him free. And part of that is opposing defenses planning to stop the run. Miami has had success this year, averaging 131 rushing yards per game, and they have topped 100 yards in five of seven games, including one game over 150 yards and another over 200 yards. They also have two games with 74 yards rushing each. Boom or bust. The offensive line—especially last week with Kadyn Proctor out with a concussion—still has work to do to come together as a unit. I think play calling is part of it, but not necessarily because the plays are wrong, but rather because the player is wrong. The rushing attack was built for Achane's skill set, complemented by Gordon. Now, it is a Gordon-led unit and some of the designs are clearly meant for Achane's speed over Gordon's power. We have seen that evolve as Slowik has adjusted to Gordon, but there is an obvious difference between the two players and there will likely be a boom or bust aspect to the Dolphins' ground game all season. The outside zone, stretch concepts were designed for Achane's elite sideline-to-sideline track speed. Gordon is a one-cut, downhill runner. The Dolphins have pivoted to more gap and inside-zone looks to match Gordon's style, but until defenses are forced to back out of the box, stops will linger. 4. Hafley brings his decades of experience coaching defense to Miami, and the numbers related to personnel deployment and coverage usage are pretty interesting through eight weeks. Miami lines up in base personnel 51.7% of snaps, second-most in the NFL, and they're utilizing zone coverage 78.8% of the time (10th in the NFL). How much of these numbers overlap with the talent available on the current roster? In other words, does it feel like Hafley's trying to put his players in the best spots to succeed? Numbers suggest the run defense is bordering on being a top-10 unit, but the pass defense might be the worst in the league. Do those numbers tell the whole story? Hafley definitely relies on base defense and he expects his front four to create pressure, rather than relying on the blitz—especially when compared to someone like Brian Flores, a former Dolphins head coach, and his blitz heavy defense. Hafley expects the pressure to come from the front four, allowing him to keep additional players back in coverage or focused on the run. It has been successful—at least as successful as can be expected with the younger players executing on the field. The run defense has been strong for much of the year. There have been mistakes, especially when an edge rusher bites on a play action, chasing the quarterback and failing to set the edge or runs right past the ball carrier, but overall, they are doing well against the run. Of course, I say all of that knowing full well Jahmyr Gibbs is second in the league in rushing and is averaging nearly five-yards-per-carry, so the pressure is on the defense to continue to find success this week. Does the contrast between the pass defense and the run defense tell the entire story? Not necessarily. The heavy zone scheme with the younger defensive backs is designed to prevent explosive, 60+ yard plays. That is allowing for short and intermediate routes to pick apart defenses (especially when Miami struggles to cover tight ends. Good thing the Lions are not bringing a top-tier tight end into this game, right?!?). Add in that Miami has been playing from behind for much of the year, and the short, possession passing game has been highly effective. I do think Hafley is keeping his defensive calls a little more basic than maybe we will see from him in the next few years, allowing the foundation to be set before he starts building off of it. The Dolphins have stressed that they expect to build for the future through the draft and grow the team from within. If they stick to that plan, I think you will see both the offense and defense evolve as the players grow and Miami moves from a roster dominated by rookies to one with veterans hitting their prime supported by key rookies each year. 5. The Dolphins opened as 7-point home underdogs over at FanDuel Sportsbook heading into this Week 9 matchup against the Lions. What's one thing you want to see, what's one thing you need to see, and one thing you're sure you'll see happen in this matchup between the Lions and Dolphins on Sunday afternoon? I want to see the offense be aggressive and take shots downfield. The Lions are allowing 276 yards per game through the air, and they are banged up. Let Willis test them early, get Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell into the game, and use the play-action to create opportunities. The Dolphins need to come into this game feeling like they have to win in a shoot-out. If they are aggressive on offense, maybe they can catch the Lions a little flat-footed at the start. I need to see the Dolphins continue to make adjustments week-to-week, correct mistakes from the last game, and grow as a unit. That will be true throughout this season. Contin

away.headline: NFL-Lions report positive progress for linebacker Campbell after injury
away.blurb: "Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time," the team said in a statement. Nov 2 (Reuters) - Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital, the NFL team said on Monday, a day after he was carried off the field with a frightening injury during a game against the Minnesota Vikings. Campbell lay motionless on the ground after levelling a hit on Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson early in the fourth quarter at Ford Field and was taken to hospital after medical staff removed him from the field. The Pro Bowl linebacker, a captain for the team this season, was drafted by the Lions in the first round three years ago and coach Dan Campbell described him as the consummate teammate. "You get voted captain, that says a ton," said coach Campbell. "He earned every bit of that. He's trustworthy, he's dependable, he'd give you the shirt off his back. He's just all heart, man, all effort." (Reporting by Amy Tennery in New YorkEditing by Christian Radnedge)

Lions coach Dan Campbell said he doesn’t expect cornerback D.J. Reed (hip), edge defender D.J. Wonnum (concussion protocol) and center Cade Mays (ankle) to play against the Dolphins. Neither of those three were at Friday’s practice. Brian Branch has practiced all week, and Campbell believes they’ll have him Sunday. Now, backup running back Sione Vaki is someone to watch when the game designations drop on Friday afternoon. Vaki was not spotted during the open viewing window of Friday’s practice. Vaki has not been on the injury report all week. He’s also fresh off the best showing of his career. Vaki ran 11 times for 65 yards against the Minnesota Vikings, and sounded like he earned a ton of trust in the process. It’s the most touches and rushing yards he’s had in three seasons in Detroit. “Again, we’ve talked about here, you always want your second running back to touch the ball and affect the game for a number of different reasons,” offensive coordinator Drew Petzing said of Vaki this week. “But then as you start having success and you see his energy and his momentum, there’s definitely that like, ‘Oh, we’re rolling a little bit. I’ve got to keep this guy going.’ And I think he brought that spark a little bit, just the way he was finishing runs, running through contact. You could see him getting up with a little bit of motion. “I think the fans got behind him a little bit. And I can’t say that didn’t lead to another carrier or two. away.headline: Lions down multiple starters vs. Dolphins; St. Brown questionable
away.blurb: Safety Kerby Joseph (knee) and linebacker Jack Campbell (neck) were ruled out, as well. Wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib), running back Jacob Saylors (neck) and running back Sione Vaki (ankle) are all questionable. Vaki, who had a career-high 65 rushing yards in a 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings , was a late addition to the injury report after not being spotted at Friday's practice. On a positive note, safety Brian Branch (concussion) is expected to be available for the road contest at Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 8. He was removed from the injury report on Friday. As for what the Lions will do at the defensive end spot opposite of Aidan Hutchinson, Derrick Moore and Eric O'Neill stand out as options for increased roles. Campbell also mentioned undrafted rookie Anthony Lucas, who is currently on the practice squad. Jack Campbell was transported to Henry Ford Hospital after he got hurt against the Vikings. He put out a statement through the team Wednesday , saying he has "full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body." St. Brown said Thursday, "I'm a little banged up, but I'll be all right." Without Reed, expect the Lions to lean on some combination of Roger McCreary, Rock Ya-Sin, Khalil Dorsey and Ennis Rakestraw Jr. on the outside. McCreary began the season as a reserve but has started every game since Week 3. Over the last two weeks, Ya-Sin (38 snaps), Dorsey (35) and Rakestraw (22) have held defensive responsibilities. "The good news is, man, we've got a pretty steady room — that is improving — of defensive backs. ... I just feel like these guys are starting to play pretty good football for us. ... I like where we're at," Campbell said Friday, Nov. 6. "Depth wise, it's a pretty strong room. I don't like the thought of not having Reed, but at the same time, I'm encouraged. I think we'll be OK here." "I mentioned this before, Brad (Holmes)'s done a good job with the depth that we've got," Campbell said. "We'll be able to weather the storm, and those guys are gonna get an opportunity. Adversity hits with injuries, that's the tough part. But the encouraging part is now guys get new opportunities, there's new guys now. You get your chance. What are you gonna do with it? That's encouraging because that's gonna help us grow." Mays will be replaced in the starting lineup by Juice Scruggs. Dan Campbell had a small update on linebacker Jack Campbell, who was carted off the field Nov. 1 . Asked how the team is doing mentally, given the linebacker's injury, Dan Campbell said, "I think every day we've gotten better. We're getting a better handle on this, Jack continues to improve, which is all great news. "This is about, man, how would he prepare, how would he play? Those are the standards for us going into this game. We owe it to him." We may earn a commission when you buy through links on this page.
