away.headline: Lions, Dolphins week 9 injury designations: Lions rule out 5 starters
away.blurb: Mays is dealing with a low ankle sprain, which typically keeps players out at least a week, and potentially as long as a month, so him being ruled out of this game was expected. How quickly he recovers is still to be determined, but the Lions have been highly fortunate to have Juice Scruggs stepping into the starting center role, and they’ve been planning on him starting since the beginning of this week. Wonnum is still working through the NFL’s concussion protocols and won’t be able to return in time for this game. With head injury recovery times varying by individual, it’s unclear how long he will need before he is cleared. Second-round rookie Derrick Moore is expected to increase his role in Wonnum’s absence, and Campbell is seeing improvement: Jack Campbell continues to improve, per Dan Campbell, but he should be considered out indefinitely until otherwise clarified. Joseph is looking “better than anticipated,” according to safeties coach Jim O’Neil, but Campbell made it clear earlier in the week that the plan was to keep him out for another game, then continue to ramp up his participation levels next week, as he nears a return. Vaki was unexpectedly absent from Friday’s practice and has been given a questionable designation heading into this weekend’s game. Beyond that, the extent of his injury is unknown, and we may have to wait until Saturday—to see if he travels with the team—or even game time on Sunday, to find out his availability. Saylors has dealt with a neck injury for two weeks and couldn’t finish Week 7’s game against the Vikings because of it. Look for the Lions to be cautious in his return, but with Vaki also questionable, the Lions could end up with a depth issue at running back. Ogbongbemiga was estimated to have been a limited participant on Wednesday and a full participant after that, and with him not carrying an injury designation, he should be good to go, giving the Lions special teams work and linebacker depth. The Detroit Lions (5-2) and Miami Dolphins (1-6) have declared their Week 9 injury designations, and the Lions will be missing multiple starters, including one on offense, three on defense, and one not yet cleared from his injury list—all of which we knew ahead of time, based on coach Dan Campbell’s comments throughout the week. Let’s look at Friday’s practice report and get you up to date on what we know. Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded . Mays will be replaced in the starting lineup by Juice Scruggs. Dan Campbell had a small update on linebacker Jack Campbell, who was carted off the field Nov. 1 . Saylors has dealt with a neck injury for two weeks and couldn’t finish Week 7’s game against the Vikings because of it. They will have to beat the 2-5 New Orleans Saints to do that and hopefully gain some ground in the AFC North. This is a winnable game, and to expect the Browns to win is not a bold opinion. If you want some sort of bold prediction, then we have those too. A forecast that goes beyond that of normal expectations, but also stays in the realm of reality. Here are my three bold predictions for the Browns against the Saints. KC Concepcion rushing score The Saints do not have a good run defense (ranked 29th in rushing yards allowed). I expect the Browns to lean heavily into their running game. This would be especially true if backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders is starting. I expect that Concepcion will be very involved in the passing game. I also think the Browns will look for creative ways to get him touches considering how elusive and explosive he is. Don't be surprised if he finds the end zone on an end-around or a backward pass type play. Judkins goes off I won't go as far as to say that Quinshon Judkins will have his best day of the year because I don't think he outdoes what he did versus the Titans. However, I don't think this game will be way off from that in terms of production. As stated before, the Saints have a bad run defense. It makes sense to take the ball out of the hands of a backup quarterback and run the ball early and often. Look for a 100-yard day and a score from Judkins. Shough-ing turnovers There is no debate that the Browns defense has been their strength this year. They rank 13th in points allowed per game and 13th in total turnovers forced. This pairs with the Browns' advantage, as the Saints are 6th in the NFL in most giveaways. I won't go as far as to predict a turnover fiesta this weekend, but I will predict that Saints Quarterback Tyler Shough has at least two in this game. The Browns are currently in third place within the AFC North division, with the team still thinking about a possible playoff run. While the loss to the Steelers was very disappointing for the Browns, the team still has the utmost confidence as it enters the game this week. However, the Browns will likely be playing the game with backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders, with starter Deshaun Watson dealing with a concussion. It remains to be seen if Sanders will be starting the game, but at this point, it's trending toward happening . Sanders did play last season for the Browns, going 3-4 as a starter at the end of the year. Cleveland's defense has the talent to keep them in this game, but the offense is likely going to have to win it. For the Browns, whoever is under center will be tasked with getting this team back on track. The offense has sputtered over the last few weeks, and this is an area that Cleveland wants to get back going strong. New Orleans can be a sneaky team, even with their lackluster record on the season, with them having beaten the Baltimore Ravens, with a healthy Lamar Jackson at quarterback, and New York Giants this year. The Saints were expected to be better than where they currently are, so the Browns will need to be careful. away.headline: Browns make big Shedeur Sanders announcement for Week 9 amid Deshaun Watson's injury
away.blurb: The Browns will start Sanders, even though Watson has yet to be ruled out for Week 9. He hasn't practiced much this week, and even if he does somehow clear concussion protocol, the Browns will roll with Sanders as the starter for one week. Cleveland could give Sanders the Week 9 and Week 10 start before the team's Week 11 bye, where they could figure out who should be the starting QB for the remainder of the year. Browns make big Shedeur Sanders announcement for Week 9 amid Deshaun Watson's injury | Sporting News Skip to main content SN 140 Horse Racing Horse Racing Latest News More Sports More Sports Latest News Fantasy Fantasy See More Football News Betting Betting See More Explore Betting Home Predictions Prediction Markets See More Explore Predictions Home Watch Watch How to Watch Streaming Services Apple TV Patrick Gorski/Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The Cleveland Browns are heading into their Week 9 matchup with a 5-3 record, looking to keep pace with the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers in the AFC North. But thanks to Deshaun Watson landing in concussion protocol, there is some uncertainty at the quarterback position for this upcoming game against the New Orleans Saints . Todd Monken cleared the air on the QB situation on Friday, as Mary Kat Cabot of Cleveland.com reports that Monken announced Shedeur Sanders will be the team's starting quarterback for Week 9. Shedeur Sanders announced as Week 9 starter for Browns "Browns Shedeur Sanders will start at quarterback vs. the Saints, Todd Monken announced," Cabot reports. This is some major news for the Browns, though it isn't a huge surprise, as a player clearing concussion protocol in the same week they were put on it doesn't happen very often. Sanders will now get a prime opportunity to prove himself worthy of being the starting quarterback this season. Considering Watson hasn't exactly been playing at a super high level, Sanders could make a real case to keep the starting job in Week 9. He will go up against a very leaky Saints defense that has allowed plenty of teams to put up very big offensive days. MORE : Joe Burrow joins rare NFL history with six touchdowns despite three interceptions With Harold Fannin Jr., Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson, Denzel Boston, and KC Concepcion, Sanders has a much better supporting cast this season than he did for much of last year. Sanders is the Browns' Week 9 starter against the Saints, which will be his first real chance to play in his second NFL season after a Pro Bowl rookie year. The Cleveland Browns have "no plans" to move quarterback Shedeur Sanders ahead of the trade deadline, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler . Sanders has sat behind Deshaun Watson on Cleveland's depth chart this season, although he's set to make his first start of the year against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday as Watson remains in concussion protocol. home.headline: Former Saints fifth-round pick signs with Chiefs practice squad
home.blurb: Former New Orleans Saints wide receiver was signed by the Kansas City Chiefs on Thursday. This was first reported by KPRC2's Aaron Wilson late Thursday afternoon. Wilson reports that Kansas City is initially adding Means to their practice squad. The 5-2 Chiefs host the New York Jets this Sunday. Means, 25, was a fifth-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft by the Saints. He started his collegiate career with the Tennessee Volunteers in 2019 before playing two years with the Louisiana Tech Bulldogs and the last two for the Pitt Panthers . Means led the Panthers with 721 yards on 41 receptions during the 2023 campaign. As a rookie in New Orleans, Means had 9 receptions for 118 yards and a score in seven games. However, he'd miss the last nine outings of his rookie year with an ankle injury. A separate ankle injury during 2025 training camp with the Saints cost him all of last season. Means rebounded to have a strong training camp in New Orleans this summer. It wasn't enough though, as the Saints released the wideout during final cuts. After being released by the Saints, Means was signed to the Cleveland Browns practice squad. He had remained there for the first eight games of this year without being elevated to the active roster. On November 3, the Browns released Means with an injury settlement. Two days later, he signed with Kansas City. This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: Former Saints fifth-round pick signs with Chiefs practice squad

home.headline: Saints First-Round Pick Could Make NFL Debut in Week 9
home.blurb: 10 Loading video... By Aaron Becker 0 Share Newsweek is a Trust Project member See more of our trusted coverage when you search. Prefer Newsweek on Google to see more of our trusted coverage when you search. New Orleans Saints first-round rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson finally made his return to practice this week after spending the first eight weeks of the season on injured reserve with a Grade 2 right hamstring strain. It turns out there is a very real chance he makes his NFL debut against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, too. According to Camryn Justice of News 5 Cleveland , the Saints are officially listing Tyson as questionable after being a limited participant for the past three days. NFL insider Adam Schefter of ESPN reported earlier this week that Tyson's return is imminent and could come as early as this week, so only time will tell if the rookie has made enough strides to make his much-anticipated return. The Saints selected Tyson with the No. 8 overall pick in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft out of Arizona State, where he recorded 136 catches for 1,812 yards and 18 touchdowns from 2024-25. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, the Dolphins stifle Jared Goff and the roaring Lions offense Michael Owens/Getty Images Anything can happen in the National Football League, and the kickoff to Week 9 of the 2026 season certainly solidified that idea. The Baltimore Ravens defense entered Week 9 on a 12-game streak of not allowing a 50-yard play, but they allowed two to the Jacksonville Jaguars in the first half of a 33-10 "Thursday Night Football" home defeat. It's also incredibly stunning that Ravens running back Derrick Henry has run for under 60 yards in four consecutive games. However, he did surpass Pro Football Hall of Famers LaDainian Tomlinson and Jerome Bettis for seventh on the all-time rushing list Thursday night. It's also a good thing Baltimore traded for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett this week because the Ravens have now scored 14 or fewer points in four straight games for the first time in Ravens history. What other shocking events could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 9 menu of games? Let's take a look at five bold predictions. Joe Milton-led Eagles upset first-place Giants The New York Giants (4-2-1) are 3.5-point road favorites at the Philadelphia Eagles (2-6), per DraftKings Sportsbook, marking the first time they are favored over the back-to-back NFC East champs since 2016. It makes sense: The Eagles have lost six in a row, and the Giants have gone three consecutive divisional games without a loss. However, the Eagles will snap their losing streak on Sunday behind new starting quarterback Joe Milton III . Milton, who was Dak Prescott's backup with the Dallas Cowboys since 2025, was scooped up off of the Cowboys' practice squad by Philadelphia. He will take his turn at the wheel of the Eagles' offense after Tanner McKee lost all three of his starts this season. Milton will bring big plays back to Philadelphia's offense. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer has compared Milton's arm strength to that of Brett Favre , whom he coached with the New York Jets in 2008. This preseason, Milton showed significant strides in the accuracy and touch departments in Dallas' three exhibition games in 2026. He completed 29 of his 43 passes (67.4%) for 378 yards, three passing touchdowns and no interceptions for a 118.2 passer rating. Milton will use the lessons he learned from Prescott to emerge victorious over a Giants team Prescott has dominated throughout the course of his career. Vikings sack Bills QB Josh Allen more than five times Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores YOLO defense leads the NFL in the following statistics: Scoring defense (13.3 points per game allowed) Red zone defense (25% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-line defense (37.5% goal-line touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (56.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (4-8) Sack rate (11%) QB pressure rate (46%) Blitz rate (73.6%, the highest by any team in the 21st century) They are bad news for any offense, but especially a Buffalo Bills offensive line that is allowing a 38% quarterback pressure rate, the 11th-highest in the league this season. Bills 2024 NFL MVP quarterback Josh Allen has a propensity for going haywire in primetime against the league's top defenses. In the Week 12 edition of "Thursday Night Football" at the Houston Texans last season, Allen absorbed a career-high eight sacks. Playing on the road in Minnesota on "Monday Night Football" in Week 9 against Flores' ferocious pass rush group could lead to a slightly similar disaster. The Vikings will sack Allen over five times, something that has happened to him just four times in his nine-season NFL career. Cowboys hold the Colts to under 20 points The Cowboys' (3-5) defense hasn't recovered from trading away All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers less than a month away from the start of the 2025 season. Dallas has allowed 29 points per game since 2025, making them the second-highest-scoring defense in the entire league. That figure is driven by the Cowboys allowing 20-plus points in 15 consecutive games, the longest active streak in the NFL. However, they will go on the road and hold the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) to under 20 points on Sunday. Indianapolis is fresh off a 42-7 defeat at the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8, and they have scored 10 or fewer points in consecutive games for the first time since 2022. Facing a familiar face in Colts quarterback Daniel Jones , whose 68.7 passer rating is the worst in the league this season, the Cowboys will finally hold a team under 20 points for the first time since Week 11 of the 2025 season. Jets' Braelon Allen goes off against Chiefs New York appeared to suffer a major blow when Jets running back Breece Hall , whom the team extended on a three-year, $43.5 million contract this offseason, went down in Week 3 with a quadriceps injury. However, 2024 fourth-round pick Braelon Allen slid into the Jets starting running back spot and has balled out ever since. Allen's 504 rushing yards in the five games since Hall's injury are the second most in the entire NFL behind only Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving's 548. Despite the 5-2 Kansas City Chiefs allowing the eighth-fewest rushing yards per game (96.3) in the NFL this season, Allen will go off for over 100 once again to become the first Jet with five consecutive games with 100-plus scrimmage yards since running back Thomas Jones in 2008. Dolphins hold Lions QB Jared Goff to under 200 passing yards The Detroit Lions (5-2) are soaring this season, leading the NFL in total offense (395.4 total yards per game) and ranking third in scoring offense (29.0 points per game). Quarterback Jared Goff is at the center of that success. Goff is averaging 280.6 passing yards per game (third in the NFL) with 15 passing touchdowns (tied for fifth in the NFL) and just one interception. Goff is the fourth quarterback to have those numbers through the first seven games of a season, joining Tom Brady (2015 and 2016), Alex Smith (2017) and Patrick Mahomes (2019). Goff is also third in the NFL in EPA per dropback (0.25). However, the Miami Dolphins (1-6) will keep Goff relatively in check by holding him to under 200 yards passing. The only team to do that to Goff in 2026 is the Vikings, the NFL's No. 1 defense. However, the Dolphins will do it on the strength of 2024 first-round edge rusher Chop Robinson's efforts. Robinson leads the NFL in quarterback pressure rate (20.6%) this season (among those with at least 100 pass-rush snaps), and Robinson will get in Goff's face enough to throw him off his game. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brandon Lee Gowton · SB Nation Thu, November 5, 2026 at 7:19 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Six straight losses for the Philadelphia Eagles. Can the Birds snap the streak against the New York Giants, a division foe they've owned for a long time? In order to preview this Week 9 NFC East matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Big Blue View . The earnest Ed Valentine kindly took the time took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let's take a look at the answers. [For my answers to Ed's questions about the Eagles, stay tuned to BBV .] 1 – The Giants are off to their most encouraging start to a season in a long time. What has John Harbaugh specifically contributed to this team's turnaround? Credibility. That is the first word that comes to mind. He had 15 winning seasons in 18 years in Baltimore, and he didn't have to prove himself to anyone. He has driven the Giants hard and made them believe they have earned the right to win because of what they have done. I think this piece I wrote on Tuesday is instructive. Harbaugh isn't afraid to challenge players or to step on toes to make the Giants better. 2 – J.J. McCarthy's playing time has been limited but he's shown some promise. To what extent is there confidence in him moving forward this season? I don't know that there is confidence. There are, of course, already fans willing to trade Jaxson Dart and run with McCarthy next year. It is way too early for that, though. I think the best word is "excitement." The Giants did not give up on the season when Dart was lost. They went out and traded for McCarthy, which delivered the message they were not throwing in the towel. McCarthy has shown arm talent and mobility in 5 quarters. He gives them more upside than Jameis Winston. His skillset allows them to run the offense the way they designed it for Dart. Can he keep it up? Can he force the Giants into a Dart-McCarthy debate this offseason? I don't know, 3 – Who are the some of the more underrated Giants players this season? Perhaps some for the Eagles to keep an eye out for in this game? That's hard, honestly. Rookie WR Malachi Fields is developing nicely. Bryan Hudson has taken the center job away from John Michael Schmitz. Abdul Carter doesn't have big sack numbers, but he has been hell to block all season. Deonte Banks has been playing well, really well. He looked like a No. 1 shutdown cornerback in Week 7 against Nico Collins of the Texans. 4 – What's the biggest matchup in the Giants' favor and the biggest matchup against their favor? The run defense has been hit and miss. Saquon Barkley hitting the home run still scares me. The Giants are solid against the run, until they aren't. When they aren't, they give up big plays. Other than that, the thing that scares me is that I still think the Eagles defensive front can dominate games. 5 – Who wins this game and why? With the Giants currently listed as 3-point road favorites (first time they've been favored in Philly since 2009), what's your score prediction? With great trepidation, I will pick the Giants to win. I'm still wrapping my head around the Giants being favored. They were 10.5-point underdogs two weeks ago in Houston. They have not won in Philly since 2013, and I am well aware that bad things always seem to happen to the Giants at the Linc. I have said for year, though, that at some point things have to turn around. I think this is the year they finally do. I will say Giants 24, Eagles 17 .

home.headline: Latest on DeVonta Smith, Saquon Barkley injury. Eagles coach on QB change
home.blurb: PHILADELPHIA − DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks will miss their third straight game as they have been ruled out for the Eagles game against the New York Giants on Nov. 8. As for running back Saquon Barkley, he has been cleared to play. Barkley has been dealing with hamstring and back injuries that have limited his workload for the past two games. It’s expected that Barkley will once again be on a pitch count against the Giants. LB Jihaad Campbell (quad/hamstring) S Michael Carter (abdomen) and PR Britain Covey (knee) were also ruled out. None of them have practiced this week. It should be noted that McKee is listed as questionable with a rib injury. Neither wide receiver practiced this week, including on Nov. 6. Smith has a hamstring injury that has recurred since the summer, while Wicks is dealing with an ankle injury. Buy Philadelphia Eagles tickets The Eagles (2-6) are in the midst of a six-game losing streak, their longest since the 2012 season. And they're changing quarterbacks, going with Joe Milton, whom they signed on Oct. 16 from the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad, in place of Tanner McKee. Milton, a sixth-round pick of the Patriots in 2024, has never started in an NFL game, although he has appeared in five (one with New England in 2024 and four with Dallas last season). Nick Sirianni on why he changed QBs Eagles coach Nick Sirianni explained the decision to go with MIlton on Nov. 6. "It's a difficult thing to think through because it isn't ever just on one person," Sirianni said. "Matter of fact, I think Tanner played solid. But this is just what I felt like we needed to do right at this particular moment to give ourselves the best chance to win this weekend." Sirianni had said on Nov. 2 that "Tanner is our guy" when asked if he was considering switching QBs. On Nov. 4, he made the switch. "You look through the game like we just got off of, and then you're starting to look through the game and the game plan, and as you start to put ideas down, and things are fluid," Sirianni said. "The toughest part about this is I felt Tanner did solid. I thought he did a lot of good things, so that's always tough." When pressed further on why Sirianni didn't mention the QB change during his Nov. 4 press conference, before the news broke that the Eagles were making the change, Sirianni cited competitive advantage and not wanting to reveal the change to the Giants. "I'm going to tell you what I want to tell you guys," Sirianni said. "I respect the job that you all have to do, but I'm going to tell you what I want to tell you guys because I'm always going to protect the team, first and foremost. Every second that goes by in a situation like that, that you can hold onto that information as long as you possibly can, is a little less time for the opponent to get ready for the game." Although the Commanders' 2-4-1 record is far from impressive, they remain a dangerous team that can win on any given Sunday. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn is currently fighting for his job , and injuries have plagued the team throughout a disappointing season. Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels has missed several games this season after aggravating a previous arm injury, while several other key players have been sidelined for significant periods of time. While they are 2-4-1, the Commanders still have an opportunity to win the weak NFC East. The Commanders just won their second game of the season after defeating the Philadelphia Eagles and currently sit third in the division. This season, the Commanders are 17th in points per game and 26th in points allowed. They have also struggled on third down, converting just 32% of their attempts, while their defense has surrendered too many points. Although the Commanders have been one of the worst teams this season, they have found success running the ball. Led by their dual-threat quarterback, they average 127 rushing yards per game and protect the ball with only three turnovers. The Commanders' biggest weakness lies in their passing defense, which ranks 27th in the league, allowing 243 yards per game and an opponent passer rating of 100.6. The Rams' success largely depends on quarterback Matthew Stafford's ability to effectively move the ball. Stafford is reportedly dealing with soreness in his right arm. He left the locker room after the Chargers game with a bag of ice on his right elbow. This could be a big game for Puka Nacua . Held to only 80 yards in Week 9, Nacua might have over 100 receiving yards this week. The Rams should still find success running the ball, but the overall game will depend on Stafford's effectiveness passing the ball. In a must-win game for the Rams, this news comes at the worst time. "I think just taking it a day at a time is going to be the best way that we can approach it," McVay said. "Think that's the right thing for him, and really just to see how he responds . But I think it's a real positive that we're starting his clock." Tight end Terrance Ferguson will also return to practice this week after sustaining an ankle sprain against the Denver Broncos in Week 3. McVay said it's likely that they will start his 21-day clock, but want to see how he's feeling. Cornerback Jaylen Watson aggravated his shoulder again and will take things day-to-day. Watson dislocated his right shoulder in Week 4 and missed the following game before he returned. away.headline: Myles Garrett Injury Update, Latest on Rams Star's Status vs. Commanders
away.blurb: Los Angeles Rams superstar pass-rusher Myles Garrett is set to return to the lineup against the Washington Commanders on Sunday. The 30-year-old veteran set the single-season NFL sack record in 2025 with 23, and the Rams likely assumed they would get something resembling that level of production out of him. Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters Garrett is expected to play on Sunday after NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported Garrett was "on track to be activated" after practicing all week. Garrett has not played since Week 1, as he underwent arthroscopic knee surgery and was placed on injured reserve following the Rams' season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers. L.A. made the blockbuster trade of the offseason when it acquired Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in exchange for pass-rusher Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, and 2028 second-round pick and a 2029 third-round pick. A seven-time Pro Bowler, five-time First Team All-Pro and two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Garrett was coming off the best season of his career. However, Garrett did not look himself in Week 1 after battling a knee injury during training camp and the preseason, and the decision was made for him to undergo surgery and heal up. Given that the Rams entered the season as the clear Super Bowl favorites, the 2026 campaign has been largely disappointing thus far. Los Angeles has a 4-4 record, placing it third in the NFC West, and it would not be a playoff team if the season ended today. Garrett could give the defense a significant lift if he is fully healthy and back to his usual form, though, which is ideal with winnable games on tap against the Commanders and Arizona Cardinals the next two week. The schedule gets tougher after that with games against the Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs and 49ers, and the Rams' likely hope by that point is that Garrett will have knocked off the rust and be positioned to contribute in a major way.

away.headline: Los Angeles Rams Get Encouraging Matthew Stafford Injury Update
away.blurb: Written by NDTV Sports Desk Updated: November 05, 2026, 7:53 AM EST Read Time: 2 min facebook twitter WhatsApp reddit E-mail Matthew Stafford during an NFL game. © X/@RamsNFL The Los Angeles Rams QB Matthew Stafford walking around with ice wrapped around his throwing elbow raises questions about his health. With the team already dealing with several injuries, losing another player was the last thing they needed. However, Stafford had a rather relaxed response when reporters asked about his condition on Wednesday, November 4. The 38-year-old made it clear that the soreness had not affected his work or his ability to play. Matthew Stafford speaks out on injury concern Stafford did not appear particularly concerned about the attention surrounding his elbow. In fact, he joked that reporters had only recently started noticing something he had been doing throughout the season. "You guys have been blind. I feel like I've been icing my arm every day out here, walking around," the quarterback told reporters. He then explained that some discomfort was understandable at this stage of his career. Stafford, in his 18th NFL season, admitted the physical demands of competing against younger players but insisted that the issue had not stopped him from practicing or taking snaps on game day. "Listen, I'm 38 years old, trying to keep up with these young bucks. Little bit of soreness and stuff that is not uncommon this time of year," he added. His comments gave some relief after head coach Sean McVay had confirmed earlier in the week that Stafford was experiencing soreness in his right arm. The quarterback had been spotted with ice on his elbow after the 24-9 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 8. The first injury report for Week 9 listed Stafford with a right elbow issue, but he remained a full participant in practice. That was another positive sign for a team relying heavily on its veteran quarterback. Los Angeles Rams face a growing injury list Stafford's update came at a time when the Los Angeles Rams had several other players dealing with injuries. Cornerback Jaylen Watson became the latest major loss after suffering a shoulder injury that required season-ending surgery. He was the third Rams player to suffer a season-ending injury in two weeks. Wide receiver Davante Adams was among those missing from the team's first Week 9 practice report, while cornerback Trent McDuffie was listed with a back injury. Tight end Colby Parkinson remained sidelined with the rib injury that kept him out against the Los Angeles Chargers. Stafford admitted that every NFL season brought its own challenges and said he did not spend time comparing the current situation with previous injury-hit campaigns. He said that players in the training room were working hard to return, adding that their availability would give the team a good welcome . away.headline: Rams Injury Report: Myles Garrett Returns, But Bad News Continues to Pile Up
away.blurb: While the Los Angeles Rams got some good injury news on Wednesday, the injuries also continue to pile up. Both Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson opened their practice windows as they work to return from injured reserve. However, cornerback Jaylen Watson’s season is over with a shoulder injury and cornerback Trent McDuffie was a non-participant with a back injury. The biggest knock for the Rams is Watson being placed on injured reserve and being out for the season. Watson was the team’s top free agent signing as the Rams looked to rebuild their cornerback room this offseason. After missing Week 4 with a dislocated shoulder, Watson reaggravated the injury in the third quarter of the team’s win against the Chargers. “The likelihood of it coming out and doing further damage to it is a very high probability. You could strap it, but it would restrict his movement,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Just some of the different things that we've received from our doctors, it's the right thing to do by him, even though it sucks because he's been such a bright spot for us.” “It's exciting. It's great to be able to get him back out there,” said McVay. “He'll probably take half the reps today. If you have 30 reps, he'll take 15 and then we'll see how he feels coming out of that. Hopefully, it's just a little bit of an increase incrementally at a time.” In addition to Garrett being back, Ferguson and running back Ronnie Rivers returned to practice as well. Ferguson should provide some insurance if Parkinson can’t play for a second straight week, while Rivers could be helpful on special teams. Also limited were linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), left guard Steve Avila (hamstring), and wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back). Coming out of the Chargers game, one of the big stories was Matthew Stafford being seen walking out of the locker room with ice around his right arm . Stafford showed up as a full participant on Wednesday’s injury report with a right elbow injury. picks.headline: Week 9 Preview: Can the Carolina Panthers Keep Up With the Denver Broncos?
picks.blurb: Week 9 Preview: Can the Carolina Panthers Keep Up With the Denver Broncos? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka logs his second 50-point game this season TRENDING UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers Week 9 Preview: Can the Carolina Panthers Keep Up With the Denver Broncos? | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Sue Levine, Editor Christopher Mason · Last Word on Sports Fri, November 6, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Carolina Panthers are coming off a mini-bye week following their Thursday night football loss to the Green Bay Packers . Now, they prepare to welcome one of the AFC's top teams, the Denver Broncos . Denver travels to Charlotte following a close win against its division rival, the Kansas City Chiefs. This will be the ninth meeting between the two teams, with the Broncos holding a 7-2 advantage over Carolina, including their victory in Super Bowl 50. The Panthers enter this matchup barely holding on to their first-place lead in the NFC South and riding a two-game losing streak. Meanwhile, the Broncos sit comfortably atop the AFC West and look to extend their lead against a struggling Carolina team. Both teams have their own issues. Carolina's defense has looked like a shell of itself while dealing with injuries and coaching changes. Denver's offense, meanwhile, has struggled to find consistency in the early stages of games, often waiting until the second half to hit its stride. Although the teams' records suggest a mismatch, this game presents an interesting study in how teams start versus how they finish. Green Bay Packers linebacker Ty'ron Hopper (59) is stiff-armed by Carolina Panthers running back Chuba Hubbard (30) on Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. The Packers won the game, 27-19. Tork Mason/Green Bay Press-Gazette Denver's Offense vs. Carolina's Defense The Denver Broncos are very much a second-half team, with their offense becoming more productive as games progress. Denver has generated 1,066 yards of total offense in the first half compared with 1,110 in the second half. The difference becomes more pronounced in the passing game, where the Broncos have recorded seven second-half passing touchdowns compared with just two in the first half. Bo Nix's yards per attempt also increased to 6.6 after halftime. The Panthers cannot afford to let Denver find its rhythm through the air. One way to prevent that is by generating consistent pressure on Nix, who has struggled against opposing blitzes. Carolina has had difficulty getting after the quarterback this season, with injuries taking a toll on its edge-rushing group. If the Panthers can disrupt Nix in the pocket, they could interrupt the rhythm that has allowed Denver to become more productive in the second half. Carolina must also find a way to stop the run. It is a message Coach Dave Canales has emphasized to new defensive coordinator Todd Wash . The Panthers have struggled against opposing rushing attacks, allowing approximately 140 yards per game on the ground. Denver uses its rushing attack to create favorable passing opportunities for Nix by forcing opposing safeties closer to the line of scrimmage. Running back Jonah Coleman also brings the speed to create problems for Carolina's defense at the second level. The Panthers showed some improvement against Green Bay, holding the Packers to fewer than 100 rushing yards while generating penetration from defensive tackles Lee Hunter and Derrick Brown. If Carolina can force Denver's running backs to deal with linebackers Devin Lloyd and Bobby Okereke, the Broncos could have a more difficult time creating the deep passing opportunities Nix prefers. Establishing control of the line of scrimmage will be critical to keeping Denver's offense in check. Oct 18, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Carolina Panthers defensive tackle Lee Hunter (92) and linebacker Bobby Okereke (58) during warmups against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Can Carolina's Secondary Stop Bo Nix? The Carolina Panthers' secondary faces a productive touchdown scorer in Bo Nix. However, the Denver quarterback enters this matchup with some concerning passing efficiency numbers. Nix is averaging 6 yards per attempt while completing approximately 60% of his passes. He has also thrown nine touchdowns against three interceptions. His 83.6 passer rating further highlights some of the inconsistencies in Denver's passing attack. Those numbers present an opportunity for Carolina's secondary to disrupt the Broncos' aerial game. The Panthers will need to force Nix into difficult throws and make him take risks when attempting to push the ball downfield. However, Nix is particularly effective at extending plays and creating open passing lanes with his mobility in the pocket. Carolina's inability to generate a consistent pass rush could work in Denver's favor. If the Panthers cannot pressure Nix, he will have additional time to find receivers Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle downfield. However, if Carolina's secondary can stay with Denver's receivers, Nix may be forced to extend plays and search for alternative passing windows. The Panthers must force Nix into difficult throwing angles and prevent him from creating open passing lanes over the middle of the field. Doing so could limit Denver's explosive plays while disrupting the timing of its offense. The longer Nix has to hold the football while searching for an open receiver, the more opportunities Carolina's defense will have to make a play. Nov 1, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) leaves the field after defeating the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Bryce Young vs. the Broncos' Defense The Carolina Panthers will have their hands full against Denver's defense. The Broncos enter this matchup tied for fourth in the NFL with 23 sacks. Bryce Young was sacked six times last week and has taken 11 sacks over the past two games. Young struggled to recognize pressure against Green Bay, while Carolina's offensive line consistently had difficulty giving him enough time to operate. This week, the Panthers' offensive line will have to contend with Nik Bonitto, Jonathan Cooper, and Zach Allen. All three have been among Denver's leading sack producers this season and have established themselves as key disruptors along the defensive front. Carolina will need to find ways to work around Denver's pass rush. That means incorporating quick passes, getting the football into the hands of its playmakers, and establishing a more consistent rushing attack. The Panthers do not have an elite running game, but Chuba Hubbard has shown the ability to break off explosive runs when given the opportunity. If Carolina can get Hubbard going early, it could open up the passing game, particularly through play-action. Carolina will also need to get creative with its receiver alignments. Tetairoa McMillan will likely see plenty of Denver's premier cornerback, Pat Surtain II. The Panthers should move McMillan around the formation to create more favorable matchups and prevent Denver from consistently deploying Surtain against Carolina's leading receiver. Similarly, if Jalen Coker is healthy enough to play at full strength, Carolina's receiving duo could give Denver some problems. Having multiple receiving threats available would make it more difficult for the Broncos to focus their coverage on McMillan. Ultimately, Young needs to get the football out quickly, avoid unnecessary sacks, and take advantage of the opportunities Denver's defense gives him. Oct 29, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young (9) during the game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images The Last Word The Carolina Panthers will have their hands full against a tough opponent this week. While Carolina is struggling to keep its head above water, last week's game showed glimpses of the team fans had seen earlier in the season. The Panthers made a late push against Green Bay, fighting until the final seconds despite being outplayed for much of the night. If Carolina can keep Nix in check by forcing him to extend plays, disrupting his passing rhythm, and containing Denver's rushing attack, the defense could give the offense more opportunities to compete. On the offensive side of the ball, offensive coordinator Brad Idzik needs to return to some of the principles that made Carolina's offense successful earlier in the season. Establishing the run will go a long way toward opening up opportunities for the receivers while giving Young more time to make the throws he needs. If Carolina can execute complementary football and Todd Wash's defense shows signs of improvement under its new leadership, the Panthers could make this a competitive matchup. However, beating Denver will require four quarters of consistent football. Carolina cannot afford another slow start or a second-half collapse. Against a team that has made a habit of getting better as games progress, the Panthers will need to put together their most complete performance in weeks. away.headline: Broncos' Week 9 Injury Report: S Brandon Jones Trending Toward Inactive
away.source: Denver Broncos On SI on MSN
away.blurb: Denver Broncos starting safety Brandon Jones was among three players who missed practice for a second consecutive day and now appear highly questionable to play in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Jones suffered a hamstring injury in last week's victory over the Chiefs and has yet to resume practicing. Ditto for defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike, whose shoulder issue has held him out. Ditto for cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, who's dealing with an ankle affliction. Each player will need to get in at least a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up at Carolina. In more fortunate news, Denver's other starting safety, Talanoa Hufanga, was upgraded from DNP (Did Not Practice) to a limited participant on Thursday, giving him a shot at returning after being sidelined for the last three games with his own ankle malady. WRs Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Pat Bryant (ankle) were full participants, as well. Bryant will return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury. On Carolina's side, five players did not practice: OLBs Jaelan Phillips and Trevis Gipson, CB Will Lee, OG Damien Lewis, and LB Bobby Okereke. Quarterback Bryce Young (ankle) was a full participant and will play against the Broncos. Assuming Jones is ruled out, Taylor Rapp would likely fill in as a starting safety at Carolina. If Hufanga can't go, Devon Key or JL Skinner would slot in next to Rapp. Skinner, in particular, had a standout game in last week's comeback victory over the Chiefs . Assuming Abrams-Draine is out of commission, second-year CB Jahdae Barron could see an uptick in snaps behind CBs Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja'Quan McMillian. Wide receiver Courtland Sutton and defensive end Zach Allen were also upgraded to full following a veteran rest day on Wednesday. Both will be active in Week 9. “You’ve definitely seen his ascension, and he’s very comfortable with what they’re doing," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Young on Wednesday. "It’s an explosive team. I think they’re seventh or eighth in explosives. They do a great job mixing the play action, the ‘RPO’ (Run-Pass Option) game. They’ve drafted well. So all those numbers are different today than they were two years ago.” Assuming Uwazurike is scratched, Sai'vion Jones would likely be penciled in as a starting DE opposite Allen, with third-round rookie DL Tyler Onyedim a possibility to make his NFL debut. away.headline: Broncos injuries: Zach Allen and 3 others cleared to play
away.blurb: Allen went down in the fourth quarter of last Sunday's 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals and appeared to be favoring his right hamstring. He was able to walk off the field into the team's blue medical tent, but did not return to the game. Allen finished the game standing on the sideline without his helmet as Denver closed out a win. After the game, Allen was asked about the injury and said, "Yeah, I'll be fine. Yeah, I'll be good." He was listed as questionable for today's game on Friday's injury report. Allen (and all of the players listed as questionable) are active and set to play against the Chiefs today. Denver Broncos defensive lineman Zach Allen ( hamstring ) is active for Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Allen has been one of the best interior defensive linemen in the NFL this season, totaling 24 tackles, 19 quarterback hits, 4.5 sacks, two pass breakups and one forced fumble through seven games. He's well on his way toward earning another first-team All-Pro nod after securing the first such honor of his career last season. The Broncos ' defensive line rotation this season has been led by Allen ( 343 snaps ), Malcolm Roach ( 283 ), Eyioma Uwazurike ( 272 ) and D.J. Jones ( 220 ). home.blurb: The Denver Broncos got a bit of a boost to start practice this week with wide receiver Pat Bryant being designated to return from injured reserve . He could play as early as this Sunday and was a full participant. There are several players who were held out today: Kris Abrams Draine, Talanoa Hufanga, Brandon Jones, and Eyioma Uwazurike were all non-participants. The biggest concern there is that Denver could be down both starting safeties in this game against the Carolina Panthers. While the reserve players had a fantastic game against the Kansas City Chiefs last week, it is always a concern when your best players are not out there each week. Given Hufanga's situation, I would guess they keep him out this game and just plan to have him make his return after the bye week. And I'm a bit intrigued by one of the worst NFL games on Sunday's schedule when Houston (2-5) visits the Los Angeles Chargers (0-7). Pretty much everyone expected both teams to be AFC contenders just like they were last year, but it has been a disaster for each club. In fact, this matchup will make league history with just how dramatically each franchise has fallen on its face in 2026. picks.headline: Chargers-Texans Game Preview: Can 2 returning starters on offense make the difference?
picks.blurb: Chargers-Texans Game Preview: Can 2 returning starters on offense make the difference? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka logs his second 50-point game this season TRENDING UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers INGLEWOOD, CA - SEPTEMBER 20: Los Angeles Chargers tight end David Njoku (83) limps off the field during the NFL game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the Los Angeles Chargers on September 20, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Michael Peterson · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 9:35 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chargers are back inside SoFi Stadium to face the Texans (2-5) this Sunday. It's been hell for Justin Herbert and the offense all year, but it's been just as rough when they've played the Texans each of the past two seasons. Houston has picked off Herbert five times and chances are they'll add to that total this weekend given how things have gone for two months of the season now. Can they FINALLY shock the fan base and dig out their first win? Will the woes continue against Houston? I guess we have to tune in to find out. Here are the three things I'll be watching the closest when these two teams take the field on Sunday. 1.) How will the Chargers offense look with reinforcements en route? The Chargers offense will hopefully look a bit different this week with a pair starters returning to the fold. Tight end David Njoku had his activation window opened this week and has logged a pair of limited practices this week. He was one of Justin Herbert's top targets through the team's first two games and I'll be interested to see if that continues once he's back. Kayode Awosika, the team's starting left guard to begin the season, also looks to be making his way back to the field after a pair of limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday. Awosika was one of the offensive line's best performance before going down with a fibula injury and I wouldn't be shocked if his presence next to Joe Alt on the left side moves the needle — in some way at least — on offense this week. Njoky being a pass-catching tight end first and forement could help the passing game while Awosika's return could potentially open up things on the ground. Now of course one player in each facet likely isn't enough to be a true fix, but that unit needs anything at all and two former starters returning to the field is a good start. 2.)Will the nightmare continue for Justin Herbert against the Texans? The last two times Justin Herbert and the Chargers have faced the Texans have been a nightmare. In last year's matchup on December 25th, the Chargers lost 20-16 in a game Herbert threw one touchdown to one interception. The prior game against Houston was the wild card matchup in January of '25 where Herbert threw four interceptions in one of his worst outings as a pro. As much as I wish I could say this is a real opportunity to exorcise the demons from those two games, I simply cannot. Herbert and the Chargers have never looked like a worse, less-cohesive unit and even with the Houston defense not its usual elite self, they still have numerous players who can make a splash play at a moment's notice. Even the return of a healthy Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston, and Tre' Harris did next to nothing for the offense's production in Week Eight. Coming out of the bye, the Chargers scored just nine points, all of which came in the first half. They were then completely blanked in the second as Herbert threw his second interception on top of nearly losing a fumble that was luckily knocked out of bounds. At this rate, nothing is going to come to save the Chargers from themselves. If they want the nightmare to end, they've gotta wake up and do it themselves. 3.) Chargers pass defense will have another tough task vs. WR Nico Collins and a rejuvenated C.J. Stroud Stroud did not have to play at an All-Pro or Pro Bowl level the past two seasons while the Texans defense was arguably the best in the league from 2024-2025. This year, with the defense taking some steps back, he's had to carry the load a bit more and that's somewhat worked out after a rough start. The Texans are the NFL's 7th-ranked passing offense and that is mainly due to an abysmal run game averaging only 84.7 yards per game (29th). After throwing for at least 260 yards in Weeks Four through Six (including two games of over 300), Stroud only threw for 153 in their loss to the Giants just before their bye. With two weeks of preparation, you have to think they'll be ready to roll. On the flip side, the Chargers pass defense currently ranks 7th in the league, as well (198.4). That rank has mostly been maintained without All-Pro safety Derwin James or veteran cornerback Donte Jackson in the lineup. If that's not the far-and-away strength of the Bolts defense, then I don't know what is. Just a bunch of names putting together a top-10 unit under a first-year defensive coordinator. Will that be enough this week?

Los Angeles is the only team in the NFL without a win and are as a result, firmly entrenched in the cellar in the AFC West. Houston sits in second in the AFC South but are three games behind the first place Jaguars. The Texans take the field following their bye week. They were last in action on October 25 when they lost a disappointing 27-21game in overtime at home to the New York Giants. Houston rallied from a seven-point fourth-quarter deficit to force overtime on C.J. Stroud’s 3-yard touchdown pass to Xavier Hutchinson with 52 seconds remaining. Stroud finished 17-of-28 for a season-low 153 yards and two touchdowns, while Woody Marks ran 19 times for 66 yards, but Houston produced only 237 total yards. The glaring issue was on defense. The Texans surrendered a season-high 188 rushing yards, including 124 and a touchdown to Cam Skattebo . The Chargers’ search for their first victory continues following their most recent game, a 24-9 loss last Sunday to the Rams. The Chargers had a 9-3 lead late in the first half but went scoreless over the final 38 minutes of the game. Justin Herbert completed 24 of 32 passes for 257 yards, but threw two interceptions, and the Chargers failed to reach the end zone for the second consecutive game. Los Angeles managed just 64 yards rushing with all nine Chargers’ points coming on Cameron Dicker field goals. The Chargers hold a narrow 6-5 advantage in the all-time series, but Houston has won the last two meetings, including two especially consequential victories. The Texans routed Los Angeles 32-12 in the AFC Wild Card round following the 2024 season, intercepting Herbert four times as Houston erased an early 6-0 deficit and ran away with the game. The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-7 after falling to the Los Angeles Rams on the road in Week 8. Now the Chargers will have a chance to face off against the Houston Texans at home in Week 9. The Texans have found their fair share of struggles this season at 2-5, but they are fresh off of their annual bye and are well-rested for the matchup. The Bolts entered this week as 4.5-point underdogs, per FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under is currently set at 41.5 points. The Chargers struggled once again when facing the Rams. home.headline: Four Chargers players have been cleared to play this Sunday
home.blurb: The Chargers’ offense, as everyone knows, has been an outright disaster. But their defense, at least in some ways, hasn’t been too shabby. They have had their moments on that side of the football, and two of their key cornerbacks are set to return from injury. Who will return for Los Angeles? Cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley haven’t played since Week 4 due to hamstring injuries. Both men were limited in practice on Wednesday and Thursday but fully participated in Friday’s session and have no injury designation, according to the Chargers’ official injury report . In his four contests this season, Shelley, an undrafted rookie out of the Georgia Institute of Technology, has five total tackles. Linebacker Daiyan Henley, who was limited in practice on Wednesday due to a shoulder injury, is also off the injury report, as is linebacker Bud Dupree, who has been dealing with an illness. Guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), tight end David Njoku, linebacker Denzel Perryman (pectoral) and wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) are doubtful for Sunday’s game. Defensive back Deane Leonard (concussion) and safety Kendall Williamson (calf) will not play. The Los Angeles Chargers will look to finally get their first win of the 2026 NFL season this Sunday when they host the Houston Texans. While the Texans boast two high-level edge rushers in Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter, they have a 2-5 record, and their overall defense has had some issues. In addition, two of their other rotation players on defense have also been cleared to play. Jackson, who is in his ninth NFL season, has been the subject of plenty of trade rumors lately. He has eight total tackles (six solo), two passes defended, one tackle for loss and one forced fumble so far this season in four games. The Chargers’ next three games could be at least somewhat winnable. After playing against the Texans, they will visit the Baltimore Ravens, who are short-handed at quarterback after Lamar Jackson injured his thumb, on Nov. 16. Los Angeles will then host the New York Jets, who are currently 2-6, in Week 11. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Imagn Images It's safe to say that last week lived up to the hype. The Detroit Lions defeated the previously undefeated Minnesota Vikings , the Denver Broncos used a goal-line stand to hand Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs their second consecutive loss, and the Chicago Bears upset the Seahawks in Seattle with some help from trade-deadline addition Jeffery Simmons . This weekend in the NFL , the Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons will battle in Madrid, Jordan Love takes the Green Bay Packers to Foxborough to play the New England Patriots and Baker Mayfield gets a shot at Caleb Williams and the red-hot Bears. Which teams should you pick in Week 9, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 4 from DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research for its hard work. Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens (TNF) Dajani ( Jaguars -10): It's tough to pick this game since we are unaware of the Baltimore Ravens ' quarterback situation. Will they be starting rookie third-stringer Joe Fagnano , or someone else? I believe the Jaguars will win, but any team can cover a double-digit spread at home. Jacksonville is a remarkable 14-3 over its last 17 games and is the only NFL team leading its division by three or more games. Trevor Lawrence leads the NFL in passer rating (112.6), while the Jags lead the league in points per game differential (+12.1). Sure, you can say the Ravens will just ride Derrick Henry , but the Jaguars have what is statistically the No. 1 run defense in the NFL, and have gone 24 straight games without allowing a 75-yard rusher. … Prediction: Jaguars 28, Ravens 13 Dubin (Jaguars -10): The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. … Prediction: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) vs. Atlanta Falcons (Madrid) Dajani (Falcons +3): I may take the upset here. I'm aware the Falcons just registered one of the most embarrassing losses of the season in Tampa, but I'm willing to overlook that given how bad the weather was. I have some questions about the Bengals. Cornerback DJ Turner has a heel injury, and Cashius Howell just broke his wrist. Then, this Cincy defense allowed the lowly Tennessee Titans to put up 440 yards of total offense last week and allowed the first Titans' 300-yard passing game since the 2023 season. Tony Pollard rushed for 117 yards and two touchdowns, so what is Bijan Robinson going to do? Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the best wide receiving duo in the league, but the Bengals may be due for their first loss in over a month. Remember, this Falcons team beat the San Francisco 49ers the last time they played a game indoors. Give me the points. … Prediction: Falcons 27, Bengals 23 Dubin (Bengals -3): The Cincinnati offense is rolling, with Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins dunking on opposing defenses. Meanwhile, the Falcons have been struggling to run the ball as of late despite the presence of Bijan Robinson (48 carries for 200 scoreless yards in the last three weeks). The Bengals do provide an opportunity for the run game to get back on track (4.8 yards per carry allowed), but Dexter Lawrence has shut down other rushing attacks before. If the Bengals can keep Robinson in check, I'm not sure Atlanta can count on Michael Penix Jr . to go shot for shot with Burrow. … Prediction: Bengals 27, Falcons 20 Los Angeles Rams (-5.5) at Washington Commanders Dajani ( Rams -5.5): I think the Washington Commanders are a feisty team that could cover this number, but don't forget that this is somewhat of a revenge game for Sean McVay. He spent seven seasons in Washington before the Rams made the smart decision to hire this 30-year-old kid to run their franchise. In his first season as a head coach, McVay lost to his former team. Since then, he's 2-0 vs. Washington, winning each game by at least eight points. The Rams are coming off back-to-back wins by 14+ points. They also could get Myles Garrett back on Sunday. LA is 11-2 SU and 10-3 ATS in its last 13 games vs. teams entering below .500. … Prediction: Rams 27, Commanders 17 Dubin (Rams -5.5): The Rams have finally climbed back to .500 with back-to-back wins over the Raiders and Chargers , and I think they can keep things rolling here by doing what they did against those two teams: running the ball. Washington has actually been pretty good against the ground game this year, but it just lost Daron Payne to a significant injury. On the other side of the ball, I don't think we can count on the Commanders' offense to produce enough points to keep up with LA's offense. … Prediction: Rams 24, Commanders 16 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Dajani (Broncos -2.5): I told you the Broncos would beat the Chiefs last week. The conversation around Bo Nix is so bizarre to me. He's not Josh Allen , obviously, but he's not worth benching either. He's not the most prolific passer in NFL history, but he's Superman when it comes to leading his team to wins in crunch time. Denver does have a great defense, which pulled off that goal-line stand vs. Kansas City, but Nix leads the NFL since 2000 with 9.1 yards per attempt when down by one score in the fourth quarter. He has 15 game-winning drives to his name, which is one shy of the most in a three-season span in NFL history. Nix hasn't even played three full seasons. It hasn't always been pretty, but Nix is pretty good in those fourth quarters. This week, Denver travels to take on the Carolina Panthers . Bryce Young 's offensive line has some serious issues, and those were evident last week against the Packers. Through Week 8, Carolina has allowed 23 sacks, which is tied for second-most in the NFL, with 11 of those sacks coming in the past two games. Plus, the Panthers' defense has allowed an incredible 42.7 points per contest in their first three home games, which eventually led to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero last week. … Prediction: Broncos 24, Panthers 20 Dubin (Broncos -2.5): I'm not buying into Nix as much as Dajani is, but I am buying into Denver's defense being able to get after Bryce Young behind what is an increasingly leaky offensive line and preventing the Panthers from denting the scoreboard. If they can keep this a low-scoring game, I like them to pull out a win on the road. … Prediction: Broncos 23, Panthers 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (-3) Dajani (Packers +3): The Packers got some extra rest following their Thursday win over Carolina, while the New England Patriots couldn't run away from the Miami Dolphins . This Packers offense has been fun to watch — not counting the ground game, which has registered the fewest rushing yards (485) by a team above .500 through eight games in NFL history. However, Jordan Love leads the NFL with 2,246 passing yards, while Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are the first duo to have 600 yards receiving each through eight games since Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill in 2022! Drake Maye has been great, having scored at least three touchdowns over five straight games, but this Packers defense will provide quite the test. Green Bay has allowed just 14.6 points per game over its last five. … Prediction: Packers 27, Patriots 24 Dubin (Packers +3): I also think Green Bay's extra rest will matter here, even if only because it will give Christian Watson some extra time to heal up from the ribs injury he suffered last Thursday night. The Packers are going to need him against New England, even if he ends up drawing shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez , as that will just open things up for Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft . Meanwhile, Green Bay's defense has been excellent for several weeks now, and with the Patriots down multiple weapons in the passing game, I think the Packers can try to make New England one-dimensional here, limiting their chances to move the ball downfield. … Prediction: Packers 26, Patriots 20 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears (-6) (SNF) Dajani (Bears -6): I correctly chose Chicago to cover in Seattle last week, and I became even more confident in that pick when the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons. The Seahawks' addition of Quenton Nelson is a great one, but I think the addition of Simmons is even better. He's the best defensive tackle in the NFL and makes life incredibly difficult for quarterbacks. In his first game for his new team, he recorded six tackles, one sack and two tackles for loss. Chicago's defense allowed just 3.0 yards per play with him

Yours truly correctly predicted the Chicago Bears to take down the Seattle Seahawks on Monday Night Football. We move on to Week 9 and we're hoping for more upsets during this weekend's action. Gilberto Manzano , NFL Staff Writer Iain MacMillan , Senior Editor, Betting Peter Dewey , Associate Managing Editor, Betting All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Gilberto Manzano Week 9 Upset Pick Minnesota Vikings (+150) vs. Buffalo Bills Josh Allen has a history of struggling against defenses as aggressive as the one Brian Flores operates. Allen did finally get by the Texans in Week 1, but that defense has drastically regressed this season. The Vikings’ defense has formed into what many expected to see out of the Texans in 2026. Minnesota is No. 1 in points allowed (13.3) and No. 2 in total defense (271.6). Yes, I do worry about Minnesota’s poor offense, but maybe Kyler Murray turns it around against the Bills’ poor defense, which is allowing 25.9 points per game. This will come down to Allen against the Vikings’ vaunted defense. Peter Dewey Week 9 Upset Pick Green Bay Packers (+140) vs. New England Patriots The Green Bay Packers can’t run the ball this season, averaging just 2.9 yards per carry, but that may not matter on the road against the New England Patriots in Week 9. New England is 20th in the league in EPA/Pass and eighth in EPA/Rush on defense, so the Packers and Jordan Love are likely going to lean on their elite passing game on Sunday. The Pack are coming off a mini-bye after playing on Thursday against Carolina, and they’ve won four of their last five games after a 1-2 start. Meanwhile, New England is extremely banged up at receiver and was in a dogfight against the lowly Miami Dolphins in Week 8 before pulling away in the second half. The Pats have struggled a bit against elite competition this season, losing to Seattle, Jacksonville, and Chicago. Will we see a similar result against Green Bay? The Packers are quietly fifth in the NFL in EPA/Play on defense, and Love has been playing at a high level all season long. There aren’t a ton of great upset spots this week, but Green Bay’s recent form is intriguing against a banged-up New England squad. Iain MacMillan Week 9 Upset Pick Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+240) vs. Chicago Bears You can win a lot of games in the National Football League if you can run the ball effectively and play elite defense, and that's exactly what the Buccaneers have been doing. In fact, they shut the Falcons out last week without completing a single pass. They now enter this week ranked inside the top seven in every rushing metric, second in opponent EPA per play, and third in opponent success rate. We don't currently know what sort of form Baker Mayfield is in, but if he's in peak form when the Bucs need him to take to the air, Tampa Bay is going to be an extremely dangerous team. I have little bad to say about the Bears, who have proven me wrong about my preseason evaluation of them. picks.headline: Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9
picks.blurb: Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka logs his second 50-point game this season TRENDING UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9 Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:49 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This is one of the most interesting and compelling games of the schedule for Week 9 and the first half of the NFL season. The Green Bay Packers are starting to find their offensive rhythm with Jordan Love improving on a week-by-week basis, but the team is still waiting for Micah Parsons to return to help the defense assert itself. The New England Patriots are in full stride at the moment. After losing two of their first three games and looking like last year's Super Bowl champions might take a step or two backwards, the Patriots have found their stride once again. It certainly begins with Drake Maye , who is starting to make a case as one of the NFL's elite quarterbacks, but it goes much deeper than that. The Patriots have been getting excellent play from their offensive line and running back Rhamondre Stevenson is one of the most dependable players that head coach Mike Vrabel has on his roster. His presence is a security blanket to the rest of the team. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) While the Patriots are feeling better about themselves on an every-week basis, the defense is also getting the job done. New England ranks 9th in scoring defense , as the Patriots are giving up 20.3 points per game. However, the Packers may be encouraged when they look at the New England pass defense because that unit is only slightly better than average, ranking 13th in the league. Jordan Love will throw for 250 yards and 2 touchdowns The Packers would like to come at the Patriots with a balanced, versatile and unpredictable attack. The return of Josh Jacobs from the commissioner's exempt list gave head coach Matt LaFleur a solid option running the ball. However, recent allegations of additional domestic violence incidents against Jacobs could result in additional discipline by the NFL. While he is still eligible at this moment, LaFleur might want to bypass that portion of the gameplan. As a result, it will be on Love to direct a consistent offensive attack, and he will be under significant pressure from the Patriots' aggressive defense. Love is one of the best pure passers in the game, and if the offensive line gives him protection, he can drive the Green Bay attack. Love has completed 192 of 312 passes for 2,246 yards and is averaging 280.8 yards per game. He has thrown 16 TD passes and 6 interceptions. He has a trio of receivers who are likely to cause problems in Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and TE Tucker Kraft. Watson's speed, route running and dependable hands should help the Patriots stay in this vital road game. Look for Love to connect with Watson for at least one key touchdown in the fourth quarter. Maye will approach 225 passing yards and 2 touchdowns Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Look for Maye to be turned on to the maximum level for this matchup with Love. He knows that Love throws one of the best deep balls in the league, and Maye wants to compete with him in all areas. While Love is also a good runner who can escape the pass rush, Maye excels in that area. Look for Maye to show off those running skill early in the game, and that will force the Packers to employ a spy who will attempt to contain the quarterback. That's when Maye will start to show off his pinpoint passing. The Patriots quarterback has completed 157 of 234 passes for 1,983 yards with 15 touchdowns and 8 interceptions. In addition to those numbers, his confidence is sky high. While the Patriots have not gotten the production from former Eagles wideout A.J. Brown, he can depend on wide receiver DeMario Douglas and tight end Hunter Henry to show off their productivity against Green Bay's eighth-ranked pass defense. Stevenson will rush for 75-plus yards and 1 TD The Patriots have one of the most underrated running backs in the game in Rhamondre Stevenson. While he is not a gamebreaker in terms of speed, he understands all aspects of the game. He runs well between the tackles and he will finish off his rushing attempts with power. He knows how to set up his blockers and accelerate at the right moment. The Patriots have TreVeyon Henderson — when healthy — to show off his skills as a speed back. However, it is Stevenson who is a difference maker and will give the Patriots the edge they need to beat a solid opponent. Patriots will outlast Packers and earn 27-24 triumph The escape factor that Maye provides will allow him to buy extra time and create more plays for the Patriots. This will allow them to maintain possession and sustain their drives. He will also get a huge lift from Stevenson, who is simply a winner and will come through when the game is on the line. The Packers will push the Patriots to the limit, but the Pats will have the benefit of their homefield, as well as their two key difference makers. New England comes away with this exciting and well-played victory.
