picks.headline: Experts Don't Like Patriots Chance to Defeat Packers in Week 9
picks.blurb: Experts Don't Like Patriots Chance to Defeat Packers in Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka logs his second 50-point game this season TRENDING UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers Experts Don't Like Patriots Chance to Defeat Packers in Week 9 (Rich Storry-Imagn Images) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 9:30 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New England Patriots were able to take down the Miami Dolphins last week, improving their record to 5-3 on the season. New England didn't play the prettiest game on the field, but at this point for them, a win is a win. With all the injuries that the Patriots have seen take place, especially to the offense, the team has been able to stay alive. This week, the Patriots will be hosting the Green Bay Packers, giving the team a real challenge on its hands. Green Bay, like New England, has started to play much better of late, finally put things together on the field. The Packers will be entering the game with a record of 5-3, with both sides of the ball clicking for the team. New England is going to have to be careful in this game; otherwise, they could be on the losing end of the contest. Analysts Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell, and Ian Hanford of Bleacher Report all made picks for the game between the two teams. But six of the seven experts went with Green Bay to take down the Patriots in this matchup. Only Gagnon went with New England to win the game, despite this contest being played at home for the Patriots. But the Packers recent play likely has to do with how confident those around the league are heading into the week. One key for New England this week will be how quarterback Drake Maye performs, especially when it comes to turnovers. The Green Bay defense can be feisty at times, using its opportunistic nature to get the best of opposing quarterbacks. Maye will have to find a way to overcome the injuries that the Patriots have seen this year, going against this tough defense. But the veteran quarterback has done well this year , even with his issues earlier in the season. Against Green Bay, the Patriots may need to rely on the running game a little more, taking some pressure off Maye's shoulders. Head coach Mike Vrabel will have to put his signal-caller into a strong position to win, avoiding any issues. The offensive line will also need to hold up in the game, giving Maye time to throw the ball against this defensive front. Kickoff for the Patriots game against the Packers is scheduled to take place at 1:25 p.m. PT/4:25 p.m. ET at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough.

picks.headline: Packers vs. Patriots odds: Opening lines for Week 9 matchup
picks.blurb: Packers vs. Patriots odds: Opening lines for Week 9 matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka logs his second 50-point game this season TRENDING UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers Packers vs. Patriots odds: Opening lines for Week 9 matchup (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Justis Mosqueda · SB Nation Mon, November 2, 2026 at 7:27 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers have opened up as 2.5-point road underdogs on FanDuel against the New England Patriots in Week 9, coming off a mini-bye after beating the Carolina Panthers on Thursday Night Football . The Patriots had a little scare against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, but were able to outscore Miami 21-6 in the second half to win 24-19. Overall, quarterback Drake Maye seems to have caught his groove after starting slowly to begin the 2026 season. Over the last four games, he's posted MVP-type numbers, combining to throw 11 touchdowns to just one interception and crossing the 110 passer rating mark in each of those games. The Packers are also coming in relatively hot, mostly off the backs of their defense and offensive passing game, and have won four of their last five games after being embarrassed at home for Thursday Night Football against the Atlanta Falcons. Both teams are fighting for something on Sunday, as the Patriots' chances of winning the AFC East drop from 31 percent to just 21 percent if the Packers beat them, according to The Athletic's playoff simulator . Green Bay's path to the playoffs mostly involves a wild card spot at this point, as the team is being given just a seven percent chance of winning the division per the same simulator. away.blurb: Now, it looks like Drake Maye will be without his No. 1 receiver once again, with head coach Mike Vrabel officially ruling Brown out for Sunday’s game against the Green Bay Packers. The fact that he’s been ruled out Sunday against the Packers isn’t entirely surprising given that he missed every practice this week. But it adds to Brown’s frustrating first season with the Patriots, and now there are even growing concerns about the condition of his knee, with some questioning how much longer he can truly keep playing at an elite level. As for Brown’s return, there’s no set timeline. He could be back next week against the Detroit Lions, which will be played in Munich, Germany, but with a Week 11 bye, the Patriots might also choose to play it safe and hold him out for that game as well. A.J. Brown went down with an ankle injury in the New England Patriots ‘ season-opening loss to the Seattle Seahawks nearly two months ago. An MRI later confirmed it was a high ankle sprain, and the team placed him on Injured Reserve soon after, costing him the next four games. His Patriots debut ended with just three catches on four targets for 26 yards. Brown returned against the New York Jets in Week 6, but finished that game with three catches on 10 targets for a mere 27 yards, and then hauled in three catches for 48 yards the following week against the Chicago Bears. But he missed last week’s win over the Miami Dolphins with a knee issue and didn’t participate in practice all week. Efton Chism III has also stepped up recently, hauling in a team-high five catches for 37 yards in last week’s win over the Dolphins. Those receivers should all have important roles against Green Bay. Not all questionable designations are created equal, and Nixon’s jovial conversation with reporters after practice on Friday strongly suggests he will be on the field against the defending AFC champions. Nixon did not practice on Thursday and was limited participation on Friday. Was he taking a rest day on Thursday? “I just hope I’ll be ready to play on Sunday. We’ll see,” Nixon said. The tone of his voice, however, took all the mystery out of it. Five players are out for the Packers, including edge rusher Micah Parsons, who was designated for return this week following last year’s torn ACL. He was limited participation at all three practices this week, an obvious good sign as he anticipates progressing into team drills next week. The four other players who are out are starting linebacker and defensive captain Zaire Franklin (shin), starting center Sean Rhyan (ankle), former starting right guard Travis Glover (knee) and tight end Josh Whyle (concussion). Those players missed all three practices this week. Along with Nixon, running backs Chris Brooks (ankle) and MarShawn Lloyd (knee) are questionable. Brooks was designated for return after missing the last four games; he could be added to the roster on Saturday. The Patriots will be without their top two receivers. Along with former Packers standout Romeo Doubs, who is on injured reserve, star receiver A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) is out. In a potential lift, star tight end Hunter Henry (foot) returned to practice on Friday and is part of a long list of players who are questionable. home.headline: Finally a Little Good News For Patriots on Injury Front: Tight End Hunter Henry Back at Practice Friday
home.blurb: “Hunter will probably be questionable,” said coach Mike Vrabel of the tight end’s status before practice on Friday. “So, anytime you lose a guy like Hunter, a captain that does everything the right way, talks to the guys in the huddle, knows what I like, my body language, route running, does stuff in the run game. It’s tough. But I know he’ll do his best to get back out there as quick as he can.” On a Friday where TreVeyon Henderson’s news about his “unexplained neurological symptoms” that have forced him to step away from the team dominated the headlines, the New England Patriots got some welcomed good news on the injury front. Tight end Hunter Henry, who left Sunday’s game in Miami with a foot injury and then missed practice on Wednesday and Thursday, returned to the practice field on Friday. Henry is a huge part of the Patriots passing game. The veteran leads the team with 29 catches on 34 targets for 326 yards and a pair of touchdowns. He’s Maye’s guy, on the field and off it. “I think he’s been someone for me that I can count on since my first snap in there my rookie year. He’s been a security blanket and a great guy in the huddle, a great leader on this team,” said Maye this week. Henry, 31, is in his 11 th season in the National Football League, his sixth in New England after five years with the Chargers. Playing through quarterback changes with Cam Newton, Mac Jones, Bailey Zappe and Jacoby Brissett, he’s been the mark of consistency in New England. He’s averaged 51.8 catches and 594.6 yards over his five Patriots seasons, scoring 26 TDs in that span. Henry has missed only three games since 2021. If he can’t go, it will push rookie Eli Raridon into a lead role and force extra snaps from H-back Tanner Arkin and reserve tight end/special teamer Cam Latu.

home.headline: Packers list three questionable, rule out five vs. Patriots | Week 9 Injury Report
home.blurb: Packers list three questionable, rule out five vs. Patriots | Week 9 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News CB Keisean Nixon, two running backs questionable for Sunday Emma Pravecek, packers.com CB Keisean Nixon GREEN BAY – The Packers have listed cornerback Keisean Nixon (groin) and running backs MarShawn Lloyd (knee) and Chris Brooks (ankle) as questionable for Sunday's game against the New England Patriots. Green Bay also ruled out five: linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), guard/tackle Travis Glover (knee), center Sean Rhyan (ankle), tight end Josh Whyle (concussion) and edge rusher Micah Parsons (knee). Both Nixon and Lloyd popped up on the injury report during the practice week. Nixon didn't practice Thursday but returned in limited fashion Friday. He's played in 76 consecutive regular-season games since signing with the Packers in 2022. "It's always concerning when a guy doesn't practice on a Thursday but, if I know Kei like I think I do, I would expect him to put himself in a position to potentially go out there and play," said Head Coach Matt LaFleur on Friday morning. While Rhyan was ruled out, LaFleur told reporters on Thursday that he doesn't anticipate Green Bay's starting center going on IR. Rhyan hasn't practiced since injuring his ankle four snaps into the Packers' Week 7 game in Detroit. Receiver Christian Watson (ribs), guard Aaron Banks (knee) and safety Javon Bullard (personal) didn't receive game statuses and will be available Sunday. Watson broke a rib during the Packers' 27-19 win over Carolina but returned to finish the game. He wore protective padding while practicing in a limited capacity this week. New England has ruled out receiver A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness) and listed seven question: tight end Hunter Henry (foot), cornerback Carlton Davis (neck), safety Kevin Byard (chest), receiver Mack Hollins (calf/injured reserve), tackle Morgan Moses (foot), safety Brenden Schooler (hamstring) and guard Greg Van Roten (hamstring/IR). The Patriots didn't issue a game status for the following players who will be available: quarterback Drake Maye (right shoulder), cornerback Marcus Jones (foot), defensive tackle Christian Barmore (illness), and linebackers Gabe Jacas (knee) and Dre'Mont Jones (shoulder/knee). ** Designated to Return from Injured Reserve - Currently within 21-day practice window **Designated for Return from Reserve List/Injured CB Keisean Nixon has been added to the injury report and is questionable for tonight's game against the Panthers news Packers list four questionable, rule out three vs. Panthers | Week 8 Injury Report WR Matthew Golden, DT Devonte Wyatt questionable for Thursday night news Packers rule out Zaire Franklin, list four questionable vs. Lions | Week 7 Injury Report news Packers list five questionable, rule out four vs. Cowboys | Week 6 Injury Report CB Brandon Cisse (hip) added to injury report, questionable for Sunday night Wes Hodkiewicz packers.c

picks.blurb: Raiders vs. 49ers bold predictions for NFL Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka logs his second 50-point game this season TRENDING UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers Raiders vs. 49ers bold predictions for NFL Week 9 Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:56 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Las Vegas Raiders arrive at Levi's Stadium with renewed confidence. The San Francisco 49ers arrive with extra rest and something to prove. Las Vegas snapped a four-game losing streak with a 38–33 victory over the Jets, improving to 4–4. San Francisco, meanwhile, returns from its bye at 6–1 after suffering its first defeat, a 29–20 loss to Atlanta. Their November 8 matchup offers a test of whether the Raiders' rebound represents progress or another temporary escape. The opening market favors San Francisco by 10 points, with a total of 51.5. These predictions envision something more explosive than that total suggests: a quarterback showcase, a monster receiving performance and a decisive fourth-quarter separation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Brock Purdy throws for 350 yards and four touchdowns Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Purdy will deliver his most convincing statistical statement of the season, reaching 350 passing yards and throwing four touchdown passes. That projection starts with a favorable matchup. Las Vegas has surrendered at least 30 points in five consecutive games, allowing opponents to dictate too many possessions. Even Sunday's victory required the Raiders to overcome 33 points from the Jets. Purdy already has 1,748 passing yards and 15 touchdowns through seven games. Before the bye, he threw for 288 yards against Atlanta despite injuries affecting several important offensive contributors. The Raiders should expect Kyle Shanahan to test their coverage communication immediately. Motion, play-action and layered routes can create uncertainty without requiring Purdy to hold the ball for extended periods. My projection anticipates San Francisco attacking through the air even after establishing a lead. Rather than leaning exclusively on clock management, Shanahan will keep exploiting favorable matchups. Brock Bowers produces 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns The Raiders' best answer will come through Brock Bowers, who will turn a difficult road assignment into a dominant individual performance. The prediction is at least 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns, including one reception covering 40 or more yards. That would require Las Vegas to build its passing plan around Bowers rather than waiting for him to emerge naturally within the progression. Quick throws would establish his involvement, while crossing routes and seam opportunities would provide the bigger gains. Kirk Cousins enters the matchup following a three-touchdown performance against the Jets, and his recent play has kept rookie Fernando Mendoza on the sideline. That continuity matters for this prediction. The Raiders can attack with an experienced quarterback rather than simplifying everything around a developmental transition. The projected game script should also create volume. If San Francisco scores early, Las Vegas will need to maintain an aggressive passing approach rather than protect field position. Bowers would become the central answer, particularly on third downs and near the goal line. His production will keep the Raiders competitive longer than expected, even as their defense struggles to match it. The teams combine for 70 points as San Francisco wins 42–28 The final prediction is a shootout that eventually becomes a comfortable 49ers victory. A 42–28 result would produce 70 total points, sailing past the opening 51.5-point total while giving San Francisco a 14-point winning margin. The logic connects the first two bold predictions, Purdy repeatedly punishes defensive breakdowns, while Cousins and Bowers generate enough offense to prevent an early rout. Ultimately, the difference will be possession-to-possession consistency. Las Vegas will manufacture explosive moments, but San Francisco will sustain more scoring drives and turn one late Raiders mistake into the decisive touchdown. The Raiders will show offensive resilience. The 49ers will show why their ceiling remains substantially higher. The Niners are big favorites in a game that's expected to be high-scoring. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , San Francisco opened up as 9.5-point favorites with the total set at 51.5. That ties for the highest total this season and the second-largest point spread. Raiders games have been video game-esque. They just beat the Jets 38-33. They let the Rams score 35 in Week 7. The Bills scored 33 in Week 6, and Drake Maye dropped 45 the week prior. Geno Smith threw for 290 yards. Adonai Mitchell was unguardable, while Garrett Wilson had a "quiet" 83 yards. It was a different story against the Rams. Kyren Williams and Blake Corum each ran for over 90 yards. Let's just say the 49ers aren't going up against the 2000 Ravens. Klint Kubiak has the Raiders' offense functioning. Ashton Jeanty was not the lead back against the Jets. Instead, rookie Mike Washington got the carries, with 25 compared to Jeanty's two. That offense runs through Brock Bowers, who had 10 targets against the Jets. Bowers finished with seven catches for 92 yards and two touchdowns. Kirk Cousins, who threw three touchdowns, has no problem tossing it up to Bowers in contested situations. Bowers has double-digit targets in all but two games this season. He's a monster, so you understand why Vegas goes out of their way to feature him. The 49ers haven't covered the spread in a couple of weeks. They've also gone under the total in back-to-back weeks. away.headline: Raiders' Thursday Injury Report Gives Reason for Cautious Optimism
away.blurb: On Wednesday, the official injury report listed defensive tackles Thomas Booker and Folorunso Fatukasi and tight end Ian Thomas as limited participants. Cornerback Darien Porter missed Wednesday's practice with a groin injury he suffered against the Jets. On Thursday, Las Vegas' injury report remained minimal. Porter returned to practice on Thursday, which is good news for the Raiders' young defensive backfield. He was a limited participant, and Thomas was a full participant. Booker did not practice on Thursday. Dont'e Thornton was limited as well. Raiders' Thursday Injury Report Gives Reason for Cautious Optimism Skip to main content SI.COM The Las Vegas Raiders are just a few days away from facing the San Francisco 49ers on the road. Las Vegas went back to work on Thursday, looking to build upon their Week 9 win over the New York Jets. Las Vegas' success this season has largely depended on the quality of the opponent they face. The Raiders have played well enough to beat four of the league's worst teams, but have struggled against the league's elite, which the 49ers are. Still, those four wins are more than the Raiders had all last season, and they are unquestionably better than last season. It may have been against the Jets, but Las Vegas aims to translate its second-half success against New York to this Sunday against the 49ers. After struggling in the third quarter all season, the Raiders' offense exploded against the Jets. In Week 8, Kirk Cousins led the Raiders downfield to score on their first offensive drive after halftime for the first time all season. It was more than impactful, as it led to Las Vegas producing their best third quarter of the season. The Raiders must continue to play well on offense to help their defense. “I think the first play of the second half might have been the throw to Brock [Bowers], and I thought that was a key play in the game and a great call by our coaches, and that whole drive, to finish that drive, it got us right back in the game, which we needed, very important," Cousins said earlier this week. “If you punt and they go down and score, it could be a whole different story. So, it’s very important, and we’ve got to be really strong in the third quarter the rest of the way. And I felt we have continued, last week in the fourth quarter, continuing to play well in the fourth quarter. But it’s a four-quarter game. You’ve got to do it, all four of them.” Throughout the rest of the season, Las Vegas needs the Cousins who showed up in the third and fourth quarters against the Jets to show up in each of their next three games. Moving forward, they will need that version of Cousins and their offense even before the third quarter. Fatukasi was a full participant as well. Based on their injury report, Las Vegas appears to be the healthiest it has been this season, as their Week 1 injury report listed stars Ashton Jeanty and Brock Bowers. The Raiders will likely give rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses a bigger role

picks.headline: Seahawks vs. Cardinals Week 9 game preview: Can Drew Lock repeat his Week 2 success?
picks.blurb: Seahawks vs. Cardinals Week 9 game preview: Can Drew Lock repeat his Week 2 success? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka logs his second 50-point game this season TRENDING UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers Alexandre Castro · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 6:14 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads A NFC West matchup always carries extra weight, and Sunday's meeting between the Seattle Seahawks and Arizona Cardinals is no exception. Seattle enters Week 9 with a 4-4 record after a disappointing 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears, while Arizona arrives at 3-5 following an impressive 33-30 overtime victory over the Dallas Cowboys. The two teams already met in Week 2, when Seattle dominated Arizona 31-7 on the road. Drew Lock started that game in place of an injured Sam Darnold, completing 19 of 26 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns. Now, with Darnold sidelined once again, Lock is expected to get another opportunity against the Cardinals. There is, however, a different challenge awaiting Seattle this time around. Arizona has made a quarterback change of its own, turning to Gardner Minshew after Jacoby Brissett struggled to close out the game against the Dallas Cowboys. The Cardinals are coming off their best offensive performance of the season Arizona's comeback against Dallas was largely powered by two players: Gardner Minshew and Tyler Allgeier. After Jacoby Brissett struggled throughout the first half, completing just 10 of 23 passes for 119 yards and throwing an interception, head coach Mike LaFleur made the decision to turn to Minshew. The veteran quarterback immediately changed the complexion of the game. Minshew completed 17 of 23 passes for 188 yards and three touchdowns, leading four consecutive touchdown drives to bring Arizona back from a 17-3 deficit. His connection with Michael Wilson was particularly important, with the receiver finishing the afternoon with eight catches for 111 yards and a touchdown, including the game-tying score with six seconds remaining. However, the biggest surprise was the Cardinals' running game. Tyler Allgeier (who would've been an amazing addition for the Seahawks in the last offseason…) exploded for 147 yards and a touchdown on just 11 carries, adding 44 receiving yards and another score. His performance was instrumental in Arizona's 33-30 overtime victory. That is an important development for Seattle. The Seahawks have had their own difficulties defending the run in the edge, and allowing Allgeier to find the same kind of space he enjoyed against Dallas could make this a much more difficult afternoon for Mike Macdonald's defense. There are still questions surrounding Arizona's backfield. Jeremiyah Love suffered another ankle injury against Dallas, while Bam Knight entered concussion protocol. Their availability will be worth monitoring throughout the week. Trey McBride remains Arizona's biggest receiving threat Even with the emergence of Michael Wilson, Trey McBride remains the centerpiece of Arizona's passing game. The tight end has recorded 66 receptions for 544 yards and five touchdowns this season, making him one of the most productive players at his position. Seattle has historically had difficulties containing McBride. His ability to find space between linebackers and safeties, particularly in the middle of the field, presents a challenging matchup for the Seahawks' defense. This becomes even more important considering some of Seattle's recent defensive struggles. The linebackers have had difficulties consistently covering the space behind them, and McBride is exactly the kind of player who can exploit those situations. If Arizona can establish a rhythm with Minshew, expect the Cardinals to look for their tight end frequently. Michael Wilson also deserves attention. Despite playing through fractured ribs, he managed to produce a big performance against Dallas. His availability and effectiveness will be important, particularly with Arizona looking to build on the chemistry developed with Minshew. Can Seattle's defensive line control the game again? The first meeting between these teams provided a pretty clear blueprint for Seattle. The Seahawks dominated the line of scrimmage, generated 18 quarterback pressures and limited Arizona to just 151 total yards. Jacoby Brissett struggled under pressure, completing only 4 of 11 attempts for 9 yards when pressured, while Seattle effectively shut down the Cardinals' running game. However, Arizona's offensive situation has changed since then. Minshew brings a different style of play, and the Cardinals are coming off a performance in which they accumulated 467 total yards against Dallas. Seattle will need to rediscover the defensive intensity it displayed in September. Getting pressure without consistently committing extra defenders will be particularly important against Minshew, who showed against Dallas that he can punish defenses when given time to find his receivers. The health of the defensive front is another concern. Leonard Williams left the game against Chicago with a stinger, while Uchenna Nwosu and other defensive contributors are also dealing with injuries. Their availability could have a significant impact on Seattle's ability to control the line of scrimmage. The biggest question: Drew Lock For Seattle, the biggest storyline heading into Sunday is undoubtedly the quarterback position. Sam Darnold will miss the game after suffering a quadriceps injury against Chicago. Head coach Mike Macdonald also revealed that Darnold played through a cracked rib suffered early in that game. He will not be placed on injured reserve, but his return will depend on his recovery. Drew Lock is expected to start, although he has been dealing with an elbow injury that limited his participation over the previous two weeks. Seattle is also preparing Jalen Milroe to serve as the backup. There is some reason for optimism. Lock already faced Arizona in Week 2, when he threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns in Seattle's 31-7 victory. He demonstrated that he can take advantage of opportunities against this defense, particularly when connecting with Jaxon Smith-Njigba downfield. Still, the circumstances are different. Lock will be coming off an injury of his own, and Seattle's offense has struggled to find consistency in recent weeks. The offensive line also needs to provide better protection, especially against an Arizona defense featuring Josh Sweat and Budda Baker. If Lock is unable to play effectively, the Seahawks could be forced to lean more heavily on their running game and short passing concepts. That makes establishing the ground attack early even more important. Final Thoughts This is an important opportunity for both teams. Seattle needs to respond after its disappointing loss to Chicago, while Arizona has a chance to build momentum following an impressive comeback against Dallas. The first meeting was a one-sided affair, but the Cardinals are a different team offensively with Minshew under center. Their passing game has a new spark, Allgeier is coming off a tremendous performance, and McBride remains a difficult matchup for any defense. For the Seahawks, the key will be controlling the line of scrimmage, limiting explosive plays and giving Drew Lock a manageable situation. Seattle has already shown that it can dominate this opponent, but doing so again will require a much more complete performance. Playing at Lumen Field should help, but the absence of Darnold makes this a far more intriguing divisional matchup than the first meeting suggested.

away.blurb: Ravens to trade for QB Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals: Report – NBC New York Skip to content Main Navigation Search Search for: Weather Baltimore lost Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to potential season-ending injuries last week. By Logan Reardon • Published November 4, 2026 • Updated on November 4, 2026 at 3:15 pm Jacoby Brissett of the Arizona Cardinals warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Nov. 1, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. There's a new quarterback in Baltimore. Days after Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley suffered potential season-ending injuries , the Ravens reportedly traded for veteran Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the news on Wednesday, adding that the trade is expected to be finalized over the weekend. Watch NBC 4 free wherever you are With the Ravens playing on Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the earliest that Brissett could make his debut for the team would be on Monday, Nov. 16, against the Los Angeles Chargers . Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will start for Baltimore against Jacksonville, with inexperienced quarterbacks Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis serving as the backups. Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and two turnovers in his relief debut Sunday against the Buffalo Bills after Jackson and Huntley went down. The two-time MVP Jackson, coming off three missed games with an ankle injury, suffered a thumb injury that will require surgery on his first throw last Sunday. His backup, Huntley, returned to the field, but he went down with a turf toe injury that will require surgery in the second quarter. Brissett, 33, lost his starting job to Gardner Minshew on Sunday. That made him an obvious trade candidate before next Tuesday's deadline, and the Ravens pounced quickly. Brissett started Arizona's first eight games this season and went 3-5 with 1,719 passing yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Ex-NFL star Antonio Brown avoids jail time as part of plea deal after Miami shooting Winners, losers as Jaguars rout Ravens 33-10 on Thursday Night Football An 11-year NFL veteran, Brissett has several ties to the Ravens' coaching staff. Quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork held the same position for the Cardinals last season and passing game coordinator Marcus Brady was a Colts assistant when Brissett was there from 2018-20. Brissett was drafted in 2016 by the New England Patriots and has gone on to play for six teams before Baltimore -- the Patriots (2016, 2024), Indianapolis Colts (2017-20), Miami Dolphins (2021), Cleveland Browns (2022), Washington Commanders (2023) and Cardinals (2025-26). An NFL analyst doesn't see Sam Darnold's absence as a detriment to the Seattle Seahawks. Darnold will miss Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals with a quad injury, and the defending champions will instead turn to Drew Lock for the Week 9 division showdown. Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Ben DiNucci wondered if that switch will actually help Seattle's offense. "I hate to say this: Drew Lock might give the Seahawks a better chance to win at the quarterback position," DiNucci said on CBS Sports' Just Football. Darnold has struggled a year after leading the Seahawks to a Super Bowl title. The 29-year-old has thrown nine interceptions in seven games, with his quarterback rating dipping from 99.1 to 79.5. Meanwhile, Lock led Seattle to a season-opening comeback win off the bench before excelling in a road victory over Arizona. DiNucci suggested that another strong showing against the NFC West opponent could create a quarterback controversy. "Sam Darnold has not played well this year. For whatever reason, he's turning the ball over. This offense looks stuck in the mud," DiNucci said. "I don't want to say this is a soft benching, but Drew Lock -- when he came in relief Week 1 against the New England Patriots -- led that team back. Played really well. High completion percentage, no turnovers. And then Week 2, followed it up against the same Arizona Cardinals team he's gonna play this [week] with 235 yards and three touchdowns. "I'm very intrigued to see what Drew Lock does this weekend. If he plays like he played the first two weeks of the season. I think this is gonna be a very interesting topic the rest of the season."

Chicago has not lost a game that Williams has started and finished this season (4-0), and it upset the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night in Week 8. Tampa Bay just beat Atlanta 16–0 without completing a pass. Chicago comes in off an upset of Seattle. The Bears are 6-point favorites, and the total is 46.5. The Bucs have won three of their last four after an 0–4 start, so they are still in the NFC South race. These predictions lean on the contrast between Tampa Bay's run-first plan and Chicago's explosive offense. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Caleb Williams leads the Bears past 30 points again Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Chicago will score at least 30 points, and Williams will account for three touchdowns. The Bears have scored 30 or more in every game Williams has finished this season, and they have not lost one he has started and finished (4–0). Since he returned from his hamstring injury, they have not trailed in any of three games. Williams threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns in a 30–24 win over New England. Chicago's pass offense averages 236.4 yards a game compared with 131.4 for Tampa Bay. That edge in the air is the core of this call. Tampa Bay's pass defense gives up 205.9 yards a game, which leaves room for chunk plays. Chicago's offense ranks 10th in EPA per play despite Williams missing three full games. I expect him to throw for at least 275 yards and add a rushing score. The one wrinkle is the Bears' backfield. Running back Kyle Monangai is listed as out with a thumb injury, which could shift more of the offense to Williams. Tampa Bay runs for 200 yards and still loses The Bucs will pile up another 200 rushing yards, and it still won't be enough. Against Atlanta, Tampa Bay ran 56 times for 324 yards. Bucky Irving gained 170 yards on 27 carries, and Kenny Gainwell added 140 on 25. Baker Mayfield attempted only three passes in steady rain. Chicago's run defense is beatable, allowing 4.4 yards per carry. Tampa Bay ranks eighth in EPA per rush, so the ground game will work on Sunday night. The problem is what happens when Chicago scores early. The Bucs average 22.3 points a game. A team rated poorly through the air can't easily come back against the best third-down defense in football, according to one projection. I'm projecting 200 rushing yards because the Bears' run defense can't stop everything. But Tampa Bay's offense needs scoring drives, not just yards, and the run game alone won't produce 30 points. Injuries make it harder. Gainwell is questionable with a hip issue, and outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was trending toward out. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka was inactive last week with a foot injury and is also a concern. Mayfield throws 35 passes and the Bears win 34–20 The game ends with Chicago winning 34–20, and Mayfield forced into a very different afternoon than the one in Tampa. A 34–20 final would add up to 54 points, clearing the 46.5 total comfortably, and it would give Chicago a 14-point cover. Mayfield returned from a fractured thumb two games ago and is still working back to full rhythm. He has 679 passing yards and three touchdowns on the season, so asking him to throw 35 times is a real shift for this offense. That volume creates risk. If Chicago leads by two scores in the third quarter, Tampa Bay has to abandon the run and put the ball in Mayfield's hands. I expect two interceptions, including one that sets up a Chicago touchdown. The Bucs will compete. They'll move the ball, their kicker has been perfect this season and their defense will make a few plays. But the Bears' offense is more dangerous, and they are better built to play with a lead. picks.headline: Week 9 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Bears have momentum going into Sunday night vs. Buccaneers
picks.blurb: Week 9 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Bears have momentum going into Sunday night vs. Buccaneers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka logs his second 50-point game this season TRENDING UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers Frank Schwab Senior writer Fri, November 6, 2026 at 11:01 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Chicago Bears hype is about to get very loud. This NFL season seems wide open. There isn't one great team yet and there are few trustworthy contenders who have emerged. The Bears seemingly saw it the same way when they traded two first-round picks for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. And through one game, it seems like a transformative trade. The Bears had a fantastic performance on a national stage, shutting down the Seahawks in a 34-17 win . Chicago's Super Bowl odds took a leap, as did Caleb Williams' MVP odds. In a season dying for a dominant team to emerge, maybe it's Chicago. The Bears' offense isn't a question. It has scored 30 points in every game Williams has started and finished (it did score just three points against the Vikings and Williams played three-and-a-half quarters, but that says something about Minnesota's defense). If Simmons has as big of an impact on the defense as it appeared on Monday night, Chicago will be looking really good. Nobody paying attention to the NFL hadn't seen how dominant Simmons is, but it was still impressive to see how quickly he fit in and made plays. Chicago gets another close-up in prime time this week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night. Surprisingly, the Buccaneers are far better analytically than their 3-5 record would suggest. They're fifth in DVOA , eight spots ahead of the Bears, and eight in net EPA (expected points added) per play. The Bears are strong in net EPA, coming in third. The Buccaneers will be completely overshadowed in this game. The Bears will be the focus on Sunday night as they've emerged as one of the NFL's most dangerous teams. That's a reason they're a healthy 6.5-point favorite. That's a lot of points, and the Buccaneers might be secretly pretty good. That's why Buccaneers +6.5 is the pick. And if the Bears blow out Tampa Bay in a big prime-time window, they'll take over as the talk of the NFL, if they're not already. The Bears are 4-0 in games that Caleb Williams started and finished this season. Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 9 of the NFL season: Bengals (-3) over Falcons The Bengals and Falcons go to Madrid, Spain, for this one. The Falcons are nearly impossible to figure out. They followed up a win over the undefeated 49ers by losing to a Buccaneers team that didn't complete a pass. That sums up Atlanta's season. We should trust Joe Burrow, who is on a heater, though there are more questions about Cincinnati's defense after it gave up 36 points to the Titans at home last week. Giants (-3) over Eagles Maybe Joe Milton III gives Philadelphia a boost and the Eagles get their first win since Week 2. But since Jalen Hurts went on IR, the Eagles have lost all three games by double digits. It's not a good team in any way, and Milton is far from a sure thing. The Giants are off a bye and should be feeling good coming into this one. Panthers (+2.5) over Broncos The Broncos are the better team. A few things work against them in this spot: It's an early start on the East Coast, and the Panthers have three days rest advantage. The Broncos are also coming off an emotional win over the Chiefs and there could be a letdown. Denver has been much better at home this season. Carolina has faded after a good start but this is a decent opportunity for a win. Dolphins (+7) over Lions Give Miami credit for playing hard. Maybe at some point that effort starts to fade, but the last time they truly got blown out was Week 2. They lost by 14 points to the Chiefs, but Kansas City led by only seven points with three minutes left. It's possible the Lions score enough to cover, but remember that they're usually a different team outdoors. Chiefs (-10) over Jets Kansas City will enjoy the breather after facing the Seattle and Denver defenses on the road the past two weeks. This seems like the type of game in which the Chiefs could take out their frustrations on an opponent that does have some talent but has won only once since Week 1. Saints (-3) over Browns The Browns are likely going with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback because Deshaun Watson was put in concussion protocol. It's not like Watson was playing so well he's irreplaceable, but Sanders has thrown only three passes all season. The Saints are well rested coming off a bye. The Saints are not a great team this season, but this might be a spot for them to get right. Rams (-5.5) over Commanders Is it time to trust the Rams? They have covered two games in a row without a sweat. Those wins came against mediocre (Raiders) or bad (Chargers) teams, but they did handle business. And the Commanders are mediocre at best and maybe just bad. Let's see if the Rams are truly back. Cowboys (-5.5) over Colts It is incredibly hard to trust the Cowboys, especially as a road favorite. But what we saw from the Colts last week in a 42-7 loss was troubling. There was no fight left in that team, which has lost key players to trades and knows its season is done. This could be a bad mistake, trusting a defense that can't stop anyone to cover almost a touchdown on the road. Taking the Colts at this point is even harder. Texans (-4.5) over Chargers It's a lot for Houston to be favored by this much on the road, however, home-field advantage has been mostly eliminated this NFL season and the Chargers have no home-field advantage — even if that was still a thing. Houston is coming off a bye and still has hopes to revive its season. The Texans still have a 34.4% chance to make the playoffs according to DVOA. The Chargers are 0.0% on that list. They'll cover a spread at some point but it's hard to anticipate when it happens. Raiders (+10) over 49ers The Raiders have four losses, and they came against four of the better teams in the NFL: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills and Rams. The bad news is this week they get the Super Bowl favorites. The 49ers should be getting many players back after their bye. But the Raiders can move the ball and they're getting a lot of points. Seahawks (-8.5) over Cardinals With all the quarterback chaos this week, we get two teams that had a different quarterback in Week 8. Brissett was benched and traded, and Gardner Minshew II takes over. Sam Darnold has a quad injury and he'll be out, with Drew Lock taking over. Lock is a reasonable replacement, and Minshew isn't facing the Cowboys defense this week. Packers (+3) over Patriots The Patriots have a lot of injuries and the Packers have a few days of extra rest. In a game that seems evenly matched, the small edges add up. Green Bay started the season very slow but has looked much better over the last four games, winning three and barely losing at Detroit. New England has also emerged after an early-season slump to win four of five. This is a really fun matchup, and even enough to feel OK taking the points. Vikings (+3.5) over Bills This is an interesting game because the teams have opposite strengths. The Bills have a great offense and bad defense, and the Vikings have a bad offense and great defense. The Minnesota defense held the Bears to three points after all; Chicago has scored 30 points in every other Caleb Williams start. It will be a great test against Josh Allen, who is having another fantastic season. It's never enjoyable to be going against Allen, but getting 3.5 points with a defense this good seems right … as long as the offense does at least a little bit. Trending VIP Halas Hall Notebook 11/6: Dealing with the chaos of Todd Bowles' defense We have our staff predictions for the Chicago Bears and Tampa Bay Buccaneers Week 9 showdown on Sunday Night Football. C HICAGO, Ill. , — The Chicago Bears are coming off their biggest win of the 2026 season, beating the Seattle Seahawks in primetime. It was a convincing win for the Bears, grabbing that early lead and controlling the game until the end. It was a huge win for Ben Johnson and his team, proving that they are legit and a real contender for the Super Bowl. Now, in Week 9 they are in primetime once again, hosting the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Tampa Bay is coming off another win, marking three-straight for the team as they are right in the mix in the NFC South. They are fresh off a win in a monsoon against Atlanta, taking a step forward to the playoffs. This is the final game before the bye week and the Bears have the chance to go to 7-2 for the first time since the 2012 season. They have all of the momentum right now and are the darlings of the NFL. But they can't overlook Tampa Bay, a team with a lot to play for and a good rushing attack. This should be another fun one at Soldier Field under the lights. As we always do, we have our staff predictions for the Week 9 showdown between the two teams. Make sure to check back with the Bear Report for complete coverage of this game and the rest of the season. Prediction: Bears 27, Buccaneers 16 I'm glad I was wrong on last week's prediction as the Bears went into Seattle and got a big win. Now, a week later they are back in primetime as they face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday Night Football. With this game left before the bye week, the Bears can't look past the Bucs. They are the better team as the betting line shows, and it's time to prove it. I think the Bears come away with a good win at home. X-Factor: Stop the run, run the ball well. The run game for both sides are gong to be key in this one. These are the top two rushing attacks in the NFL and will be a huge test for the opposing defenses. Whoever runs the ball better in this one should win. Prediction: Bears 42, Buccaneers 21 The hype about the Bears is completely warranted after the way that the Week 8 game transpired. The Bears went into one of the toughest road environments in the league and managed to come away with a big win. It's a week-to-week league in the NFL and so now the question shifts to whether or not the Bears can have a repeat performance in Week 9. The Bears are on a hot streak so give me Chicago at home on Sunday Night Football with a victory for the first time since 2018. X-Factor: The Bears DL depth. The acquisition of Jeffery Simmons instantly made everyone on the DL better but it's also important for guys like Shemar Turner , James Lynch, and Neville Gallimore to continue stepping up and making plays. Andrew Freeman Prediction: Bears 30, Buccaneers 20 Coming off a big win on Monday night, the Bears can't have a letdown on Sunday night. Tampa Bay has played better recently, so this could still be a competitive game. If the defense can stop the run, however, the Bears should have no problem pulling away. X-factor: Montez Sweat . With Baker Mayfield still recovering from his thumb injury, the Bears have to stop the run to make them throw. Sweat will be crucial off the edge in that regard, in addition to what he can do as a pass rusher. Prediction: Bears 31, Buccaneers 17 The Bears are looking unstoppable after a huge road win against the Seahawks last week and that momentum should continue against a middling Bucs team that sits at 3-5 in their first 8 games. While last week's improbable victory over Atlanta bodes well for them, Baker Mayfield will need to step up in the passing game and faces a steep challenge against a revamped Bears front seven led by Jeffery Simmons, especially if star WR Emeka Egbuka is out again with a foot injury. On the other side of the ball, the Bucs defense has fared well so far but faces a stiff challenge against a red hot Caleb Williams who dominated a strong Seahawks defense. I see Chicago winning easily in their third straight prime time game. X-factor: Jefferey Simmons. Like last week, Simmons opened up more opportunities for the defense to generate pressure and force stops. The same success this week will mean another dominant performance and sets up Williams and Co for more opportunities to score. Jackson Gross Prediction: Bears 28, Buccaneers 17 The Bears will get a chance to finish their three-game primetime streak at 3-0, as they host Tampa Bay. I think, given how this defense looked on Monday Night and another week with Jeffery Simmons, the Bears should roll pretty easily against an inconsistent Bucs team. X-Factor: Rome Odunze . He's looked so good since his drop against the Eagles in Week 3. He's caught 62.5% of his targets, 329 yards (65.8 yards per game), and 16.4 yards per catch. Despite that, he still hasn't cracked the end zone, but I think that changes against Tampa Bay. home.blurb: The Bears (6-2) went three weeks without their starting quarterback in Caleb Williams, and they have been clicking since his return from a hamstring injury. Chicago has scored 30 or more points while winning each game since Williams' return. Tampa Bay (3-5) amassed 582 yards on the ground while winning back-to-back games. "The last few weeks, we have been riding the hot hand with the run game," Mayfield said Wednesday. Tampa Bay has averaged 168.6 yards on the ground over its eight games, and the reduction of passes has aided Mayfield's recovery from a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand that caused him to miss three games. Mayfield attempted just 14 passes over the past two games, including only three against the Falcons. "It feels better and better each week, especially the last two weeks, not having to use it that much, not a lot of contact," Mayfield said. home.headline: Buccaneers at Bears: Initial injury report for Week 9
home.blurb: Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (foot) remained sidelined after missing the team's previous two games, leaving his availability for Sunday uncertain. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) also did not practice and is expected to miss the matchup after suffering an MCL sprain in the Buccaneers' Week 8 victory over the Atlanta Falcons. Defensive lineman Elijah Roberts was the third player held out of practice, although his absence was listed as personal rather than injury-related. Running back Kenny Gainwell (hip) and safety Tykee Smith (ankle) were limited participants Wednesday. Meanwhile, quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb), guard Cody Mauch (back) and tight end Cade Otton (thumb) participated fully. Tampa Bay will have two more practice sessions before the team's final injury report is released Friday, providing a clearer picture of who will be available for Sunday's contest. Can the Buffalo Bills keep rolling against the NFL's stingiest defense? Can the Minnesota Vikings generate enough offense to avoid wasting another strong defensive performance? Buffalo visits U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9 following a 36–10 victory over Baltimore. Minnesota returns home after Detroit ended its unbeaten start with a 19–15 win. The Bills opened as three-point favorites, setting up a compelling clash between offensive firepower and defensive disruption. These three predictions anticipate a departure from Minnesota's usual defensive script, explosive passing, costly mistakes and a dramatic finish that hands Buffalo its second defeat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Justin Jefferson explodes for 175 yards and two touchdowns Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Jefferson will deliver the performance Minnesota has been waiting for, finishing with at least 175 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Jefferson caught five passes for 33 yards and a touchdown against Detroit and enters Week 9 without a 100-yard receiving game. Buffalo presents an opportunity to change that. Its defense ranks 30th against the pass, making this a matchup Minnesota should attack rather than approach conservatively. The Vikings need to manufacture touches before asking Jefferson to win difficult downfield assignments. Motion, condensed formations and crossing routes would help create cleaner releases and give the quarterback defined throwing windows. The bigger gains should follow when Buffalo adjusts to those shorter completions. One double move or broken coverage could turn a productive evening into a spectacular one. Quarterback availability remains important. Kyler Murray is managing hamstring tightness , with Carson Wentz the likely alternative if Murray cannot play. Expect Minnesota to make its best receiver the centerpiece, not merely a name opponents must account for. Josh Allen accounts for four touchdowns but commits three turnovers Allen will produce enough spectacular plays to keep Buffalo dangerous and enough mistakes to give Minnesota control of the outcome. The bold prediction is four total touchdowns alongside three turnovers, including at least two interceptions. https://twitter.com/search?q=josh%20allen&src=typed_query&f=top Minnesota's defense provides the foundation for that aggressive forecast. Entering Week 9, the Vikings lead the league in points allowed per game at 13.3, quarterback pressure rate at 45.8 percent and sack percentage at 10.96 percent. Pressure alone will not neutralize Allen. His ability to escape the pocket can turn a successful blitz into a defensive emergency, particularly when coverage players must chase receivers across the field. That creates the central tension. Minnesota will win several snaps decisively, but Allen will punish a few failed pressure attempts with explosive completions or scrambling opportunities. The turnovers will come when he tries to rescue plays that should end with a throwaway. Disguised coverage behind an apparent blitz can invite exactly that kind of aggressive decision. Buffalo's offensive line also bears watching. Right tackle Spencer Brown's availability is a concern entering the matchup, potentially complicating protection against Minnesota's pressure packages. Allen will remain the game's most dangerous improviser. On this night, improvisation will carry a substantial price. Minnesota wins 38–35 on a last-second field goal The final bold prediction ties those individual performances together: Minnesota wins a shootout with a field goal as time expires. A 38–35 result would produce 73 points, comfortably exceeding the opening total of 46.5. It would also represent a dramatic departure from the Vikings' defensive scoring average. The logic is not that Minnesota suddenly becomes a bad defense. Turnovers and explosive plays can produce points without requiring long, methodical drives. Jefferson's breakout keeps the Vikings moving, while Allen repeatedly answers before one late mistake gives Minnesota the deciding possession. After losing its unbeaten record, Minnesota will respond with its most convincing offensive statement and a victory that reinforces its place among the league's contenders. And while losing the game wouldn't make them a pretender, winning the game could solidify the Vikings as contenders. Minnesota has played great defense through seven games, but the offense has been lacking. Now, fans are looking for the team to show improvement on offense. If it doesn't happen, we could see the team explore changes on offense. Vikings Wire's Andrew Harbaugh predicts that Vikings backup quarterback Carson Wentz will see playing time in Monday night's game against the Buffalo Bills. Here's some of what Harbaugh had to say about his chances to take the field for Minnesota in the game. "Kyler Murray has played poorly enough this season and has not shown a real grasp of the offense or the players' tendencies within it. Carson Wentz has not been a rockstar, but he has been more than serviceable for the Vikings when he has played. I predict that the first half could be rough for the Vikings' offense, and at halftime Kevin O'Connell tries to give the offense a spark with a quarterback change." Harbaugh adds that it could be a breakout day for another Vikings player. He has star Vikings wideout Justin Jefferson catching two touchdown passes in the matchup. Here's what he had to say on the breakout. "Justin Jefferson has started to be a bit more vocal about how he feels about the offense being so quiet. I think they make it a point to get him going early in the game, and then by the end of the night he has two touchdowns. They have to get him involved more; the offense goes as Justin Jefferson goes, after all. If they do not use him more soon, then ideas and outside voices are going to start getting louder." Jefferson's frustrations have drawn questions about the player throwing him the football. It's not surprising that there have been questions given all the pieces that the Vikings have on offense. It's not that starting quarterback Kyler Murray has been awful. The offense has been awful, though. Some believe a change at quarterback is necessary to bring a spark. Maybe a change at quarterback isn't the fix, but something will need to change for the offense to start moving the football. If it doesn't the Vikings will have squandered what could be one of the NFL's best defenses of the last decade. We'll keep a close eye on what moves head coach Kevin O'Connell makes when the matchup gets underway with Buffalo.

picks.headline: NFL Insider Makes Bold Prediction About Vikings Offensive Direction in Week 9 vs. Bills
picks.blurb: NFL Insider Makes Bold Prediction About Vikings Offensive Direction in Week 9 vs. Bills - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka logs his second 50-point game this season TRENDING UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 fantasy sleepers Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kevin O'Connell has spent the week calling Kyler Murray his starter, but a hamstring may make that call for him. NFL Network insider Tom Pelissero said Thursday on KFAN's Power Trip Morning Show that he expects Carson Wentz to start for the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings against the Buffalo Bills on Monday night, days after Murray struggled through the loss in Detroit . "I would lean toward it being Carson Wentz," Pelissero said on KFAN . He described the hamstring as legitimate but not major, and said Minnesota may not want to risk a quarterback who relies on his legs at less than full speed. Carson Wentz has already won two games Nov 1, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell talks to quarterback Kyler Murray (1) during the third quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field.Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Wentz isn't a stranger to this offense. He played most of the 39-22 opener against Green Bay after replacing Murray early and threw three touchdown passes, then started the 9-3 win in Chicago. He has 276 passing yards and no interceptions this season, and Minnesota won both games. Those wins weren't pretty, though. The offense scored nine points at Soldier Field, and Wentz was sacked six times across the two games. Behind a line that has allowed 21 sacks, the Vikings would be trading mobility for a quarterback who has to get the ball out on time. Murray has 1,022 passing yards, five touchdown passes and three interceptions, and he's been sacked 15 times. He has also run for 167 yards on 29 carries, which is why a sore hamstring matters more for him than it would for most quarterbacks. O'Connell said Monday he isn't considering a performance benching and Murray is still the starter when healthy, per ESPN. "I don't think we're there yet," he said of a possible absence , adding that he would keep getting updates from the medical staff. Pelissero's take lands after Nick Kostos argued the Vikings can't keep waiting on Murray . Pelissero also said he sees a low chance of a major trade before the Nov. 10 deadline, which leaves the job between the two quarterbacks already in the building. Either one draws a tough assignment. Buffalo's Greg Rousseau has seven sacks, and Josh Allen brings the NFL's most efficient offense to U.S. Bank Stadium, so Brian Flores' defense may need to carry the night again. O'Connell's Thursday press availability should offer the next clue. away.headline: Buffalo Bills injury report: Dion Dawkins, Alec Anderson still out
away.blurb: Ty Johnson returned to practice, but now it’s Sam Franklin, Jr. who is out with an illness. No worries, like Johnson, it’s likely he will be back tomorrow. Spencer Brown has been limited both days this week. I would expect he gets a questionable designation Saturday, but suits up anyway. The question is how long can he go Monday night without his back seizing back up. Running back Demond Claiborne was downgraded from limited with a knee injury to not practicing at all. Wide receiver Juan Jennings was also downgraded from limited with a calf injury to a did-not-participate. They had three players move from limited to full practice today: OT Christian Darrisaw, LB Jake Golday, and CB Isaiah Rodgers Not much changed on the Buffalo Bills’ injury report as they completed their second day of practice as they gear up to take on the NFC’s two-seeded Minnesota Vikings. There were a few minor changes that ensures us the Bills’ PR department didn’t just copy and paste yesterday’s report. Dalton Kincaid was upgraded to a full participant. It’s a good sign for the fourth-year tight end who is still looking to finish a full season without missing any playing time. Khalil Shakir missed Friday’s practice for personal reasons. Nothing to worry about here. Deone Walker was listed with a thumb injury for the first time. Whatever the injury is, it didn’t keep him from participating fully on Friday. Dion Dawkins missed a second straight day of practice with a rib injury. It’s an injury he says came in the first quarter of last week’s win over the Baltimore Ravens. The Bills’ left tackle said he plans to be ready to go Monday night. Alec Anderson not practicing for two days with an ankle injury is not a good sign. He was seen in a boot after Sunday’s game. I would bet he misses Monday. The question is will it be Tylan Grable or Austin Corbett in his slot. The Buffalo Bills game plan likely has a lot of James Cook in it. That and some really quick slants. Will a patched up front line be able to hold? As for the Vikings, they only had a few changes of their own on Friday’s report.

away.headline: Ravens Get Disappointing Injury Update on Tyler Huntley After Loss to Bills: Report
away.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens had a rough afternoon, starting with the first offensive play of the game when quarterback Lamar Jackson hit Bills defender Greg Rousseau's arm, causing Jackson to suffer a thumb injury and not return. Jackson's backup, Tyler Huntley , also didn't last long. Huntley suffered a toe injury in the first half and didn't return. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Sunday that Huntley suffered a turf toe injury. Huntley and Jackson could both miss time, and Jackson is confirmed out for at least four weeks. Head coach Jesse Minter said postgame that Jackson will be placed on injured reserve and will undergo surgery on his right thumb. Ravens Offensive Weapon Set to Return Thursday Night vs Jags Ravens Get Disappointing Injury Update on Tyler Huntley After Loss to Bills: Report Unlock the latest Heavy on Ravens news — direct to your inbox. This was Jackson first game back after he suffered an ankle injury against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4 and missed the last three games. "Ravens QB Tyler "Snoop" Huntley suffered what is thought to be a turf toe injury today at Buffalo, per source," Schefter wrote on X. "He is expected to undergo an MRI tomorrow to determine how much time if any he could miss." Ravens Could Be Down Jackson and Huntley for a While The Ravens turned to quarterback Joe Fagnano after losing Huntley, and he had a tough afternoon, completing 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and one interception. Minter also said, "We'll see" on whether Jackson will miss the rest of the season. Huntley has started three games this season, and the Ravens are 1-2. The Ravens beat the Falcons in his first start of the season but lost the last two against the Browns and Bengals. Losing your starting quarterback and backup in the same game is never good. It's even worse when this happens during a short week. The Ravens will have a quick turnaround as they host the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night. The Jaguars are coming off a 42-7 win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday to move to 5-2. Baltimore might not have a chance to play Huntley even if he can go, since it's hard to come back from an injury on a shorter week with less than four full days to recover. It will also be difficult for the Ravens to bring in a quarterback to play on Thursday, even if they lack confidence in Fagnano. The Ravens might have to get by with Fagnano starting on Thursday, then reevaluate options when they have about 10 days off between their games against the Jaguars and the Los Angeles Chargers on Nov. 16. home.headline: Kyler Murray Injury Update: NFL Insider Casts Doubt on Vikings QB's Status; Odds vs. Bills Shift
home.blurb: Minnesota's odds in this game have dropped quite a bit with Murray's injury, and it's possible they could move further if he sits out in Week 9. Sports Illustrated spoke to oddsmakers about the injury a,d BetMGM's Christian Cipollini, a Senior Trading Manager, explained that the spread would move quite a bit if Wentz gets the start. For now, bettors and fans have to wait and see if Murray is able to log at least a limited session in Thursday's practice. Based on the latest odds movement, he seems to be 50/50 for Monday's showdown with Josh Allen and the Bills. Kyler Murray Injury Update: NFL Insider Casts Doubt on Vikings QB's Status; Odds vs. Bills Shift Skip to main content ON SI Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray is up in the air for Week 9 against the Buffalo Bills due to a hamstring injury that he suffered in the team's Week 8 loss to the Detroit Lions. Earlier this week, Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell revealed that Murray is dealing with a hamstring issue and that he'd be re-evaluated this week. Murray and the Vikings don't play until Monday night in Week 9, so they have yet to release a practice report since their first official session will come on Thursday. That has left the quarterback's status in limbo with the Vikings (6-1) looking to remain in the top spot in the NFC North. NFL insider Ian Rapoport doesn't believe that Murray is dealing with a long-term injury, but he did mention that Murray may not play since he's a mobile quarterback and can't move around as well. That would pave the way for veteran Carson Wentz to get the start, something he did in place of Murray in Week 2. Full explanation on Kyler Murray from @RapSheet , per @PatMcAfeeShow : https://t.co/K3aaL2GVTY pic.twitter.com/da4lbmi97C "You'll see this line go back down to Bills -3 if Kyler is healthy and does play," Cipollini said. "If it is Wentz this line will probably close around Bills -6. Wouldn't impact futures at the moment, the strength of this team is built through the defense and coaching so a rare one where QB play is more of a bonus for this team." DraftKings Sportbsook had moved the Vikings to 2.5-point underdogs at home in this matchup, but the line has since shifted back up to Minnesota +3.5. The Vikings opened as three-point underdogs on Sunday night , but they were gaining ground at home before the Murray update was released. There's no doubt that oddsmakers view the former No. 1 overall pick as an upgrade over Wentz. This season, Murray has completed 64.9 percent of his passes for 1,022 yards, five scores and three picks while adding 29 carries for 167 yards on the ground. The Vikings are in the bottom three in the league in EPA/Play and success rate on offense, so Wentz doesn't have a high bar to clear if he's the quarterback on Monday night. home.headline: Vikings-Bills First Injury Report
home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray being out is the big news and he will not play on Monday night. Theo Jackson also did not practice on Thursday and seems more questionable whether he’ll play or not. Kevin O’Connell said they have other safeties like Jay Ward who could play in Jackson’s absence and a few others are possbilities to be active on Monday night if need be as well. The rest of the injuries appear to be more of the ‘playing through it’ variety and don’t seem like they’ll keep those players out on Monday night. For the Bills, a laundry list of players on the injury report including three offensive line starters. Starting left tackle Dion Dawkins did not practice Thursday with a rib injury, nor did starting guard Alec Andreesen, with an ankle injury. Right tackle Spencer Brown was limited with a back issue. We’ll see how it plays out with injury updates tomorrow and Saturday. home.blurb: In a positive development, Brown began the practice week by participating in a limited capacity, but back injuries can be fickle to say the least. Offensive starters DJ Moore, Keon Coleman and Dalton Kincaid were all limited participants on Thursday. All three skill players were seen wearing red non-contact jerseys during the media-viewing portion of practice ( h/t WGR's Sal Capaccio ). Along with Dawkins and Anderson, there were three more non-participants. Wide receiver Josh Palmer is seemingly looking at a multi-week absence after pulling his hamstring in Week 8 . Defensive tackle Greg Gaines, who was banged up in practice last week, remains out. Third-down running back Ty Johnson missed Thursday's practice due to illness. Despite being limited, and wearing a red jersey as a precaution, the outlook is nothing but positive for Moore. Dawkins was a surprise addition to the injury report as he appeared to come out of Sunday's game intact. He sat out the last possession, missing four snaps, but so did Allen and starting center Connor McGovern. Veteran guard Austin Corbett, who subbed in for the Allen touchdown rush, would start on Monday if Anderson is unavailable. Coleman is limited by a shoulder, which explains the red non-contact jersey he dawned on Thursday. It's unknown at which point in the game the injury occurred. He led all Bills' wide receivers with 63 snaps.
